hotspots.title: Hold the Academy Line
hotspots.employer: Federated Suns — New Ivaarsen Chasseurs (AFFS)

contract.constraints: Salvage cannot be raised above Exchange (nonnegotiable — AFFS intelligence claims the wrecks). Command cannot be lowered below House.
contract.additionalRequirements: Track Scale 2 or higher; minimum fielded force 5,000 BV / 200 PV.

a.situation: A Combine raiding force is in-system with no declaration and one purpose: burn the academy's cadre and wreck a Fluute factory line before relief crosses the border. The Chasseurs are stretched covering the capital approaches. Your command is the mobile reserve on the Vestfold plain — meet the raid where it lands and hold.

b.employer: Draconis Combine — DCMS raiding command (the New Ivaarsen bleeding-raid)

contract.constraints: Command House (a DCMS liaison rides with the raid; the Dragon directs the axis). Salvage Exchange (the Combine claims the Davion hardware pulled off the field; you take the cash).
contract.additionalRequirements: Track Scale 2 or higher; a fast raiding force — hit the cadre and the factory line and be gone before the relief column crosses the border.
contract.bonus: Bleed the arsenal — wreck the Fluute factory control room (Track 3) or win two of the three tracks, and the DCMS pays a raid-success bonus: +1 Reputation with the Combine and priority resupply on the pull-out.

b.blurb: Fight for the Dragon — burn New Ivaarsen's training cadre and wreck a factory line the Suns can't quickly rebuild, then lift before the relief arrives.
b.situation: New Ivaarsen schools and arms the whole March border; the Dragon does not mean to take it, only to bleed it. Land fast, burn the training cadre, wreck a factory line the Suns cannot quickly rebuild, and lift before their relief crosses the border. Speed is the plan — every hour on the ground feeds the Chasseurs' concentration.

hotspots.situation:
New Ivaarsen is a fortress with a school attached. For generations it has trained the officers of the New Ivaarsen Chasseurs, the regiment that holds this whole stretch of the Draconis March border, and its factories build the machines those officers ride to war. That makes it one of the most valuable worlds in the Reach and one of the most stubbornly defended: an A-A-A industrial world where the arsenal, the academy, and the veterans who run both sit within a day's march of each other. The Federated Suns can lose ground almost anywhere else along this border and recover. It cannot lose New Ivaarsen without losing the ability to replace what it spends holding everything else.

The Draconis Combine knows this, which is why, in the spring of 3151, a Combine raiding force jumps in-system without a declaration. It has not come to conquer — the Chasseurs are too strong for that — but to bleed. The plan is to burn the training cadre before it graduates, wreck a factory line the Suns can't quickly rebuild, and be gone before a relief column crosses the border to answer. The Chasseurs are already stretched thin covering the capital approaches, so their regional command hires outside iron. Your command is bought to be the mobile reserve on the open Vestfold plain: the unit that meets the raid wherever it lands, holds long enough for the regulars to concentrate, and plugs whichever hole opens first. Hold, and you save an arsenal. Fail, and you hand the Combine exactly the wound it came for.

contract.additionalRequirements: Track Scale 2 or higher; minimum fielded force 5,000 BV / 200 PV.

Comms jamming. The first friendly Battlefield Support each track needs an 8+ (2D6) or the strike is wasted.
Cold front. Night rules and -1 to all ranged to-hit for the first 3 turns.
Roll twice, ignore repeats.

tracks.name: The Vestfold Plain
tracks.situation: The raid lands on the open farmland east of the academy. You hold; the Combine wants through you.

You (Defender) hold one-third of your force off-map (arriving end of Turn 1, anywhere in your own half); the rest sets up within 6 hexes of your home edge (12" AS; 12/18" at Scale 2+). Delay — half the Combine force stays engaged for 2 consecutive turns.
Push Through — exit half your attacking force off the Combine's home edge.

forks.consequence: The Combine goes for the factory — the raid's real target.

tracks.name: Cover the Withdrawal
tracks.situation: The line broke. The academy is trucking its instructors and cadets west; you buy them the road.
tracks.deployment: Short edges, same-edge start. You (Defender) enter from the Combine's edge Turn 1; the Combine (Attacker) enters its own edge Turn 2.

Break Contact — exit at least one of your units off your home edge.

tracks.name: The Factory Floor
tracks.situation: Everything the raid was really about. The Combine goes for the Fluute factory line — four production halls, one the master control room the whole plant runs on. Stop them, or the academy loses its arsenal.
tracks.deployment: Long edges. You (Defender) set up before Initiative in your own half, at least half your force within 3 hexes of four Medium buildings (Level 2+, 30 damage / AS 6, -4 to-hit while stationary) near center. One building is secretly recorded as the control room (HQ). The Combine (Attacker) enters half on its home edge Turn 1, the rest from a short edge Turn 2.

objectives.text: Case the Plant — scan 2 buildings, or find the HQ.
Hold the Halls — half your force within reach of the buildings at end of Turn 4.
Identify and Destroy — after scanning it, destroy the control-room building.
Rough Up the Place — destroy half the buildings.
Seek and Destroy — kill the Combine commander (Tai-i Kurita).

At contract close, apply the Cadre-Losses -1 Reputation + Combine head-start if it hit 3+; if academy and factory both stand, +1 Reputation.

The Trial's rules are absolute — break them and the cargo may still be won, but no Sea Fox will ever again hire the blade who won it that way.

hotspots.situation:
The Sea Fox merchant Clan does not go to court. When two of their factors fall into a dispute they cannot trade their way out of, they settle it the Clan way — by Trial. Here the quarrel is over a single cargo contract: a hold full of rare boreal pharmaceuticals harvested only in Xhosa VII's cold northern seas, a shipment worth more than the two factors' pride combined. Both claim the right to carry it. Sea Fox custom says the claim belongs to whoever's champion wins on the field, so the enclave outside New Xhosa has cleared a frozen lake, set the witnesses on the shore, and named a day. Whoever's blade stands at the end takes the contract, the cargo, and — worth more to a Sea Fox than either — the reputation.

You are hired as one factor's champion. The other factor has hired a rival mercenary command, and the two of you will fight the same fields from opposite corners. This is not a war and it is not a raid; it is a duel with an audience, bound by Sea Fox honor rules that both sides must keep. No air strikes, no artillery, no ganging up on a warrior who has yielded — a champion who breaks those rules may still win the cargo but will find no Sea Fox on this side of the Reach willing to hire him again. So the fight is really two fights at once: the one against the rival champion on the cracking ice, and the one for the enclave's respect. Win clean and the merchant Clan pays generously and opens its own armory to you. Win dirty, or lose, and you leave Xhosa VII filed under a Sea Fox's least favorite word: adequate.

hotspots.title: The March Capital Holds
hotspots.employer: Federated Suns — House Sandoval / Robinson March Militia (AFFS)

a.employer: Federated Suns — House Sandoval / Robinson March Militia (AFFS)

contract.constraints: Command cannot be lowered below House (a Sandoval liaison rides with you — the capital's defense is not left entirely to hired guns). Base Pay is generous; the March pays for its pride.
contract.additionalRequirements: Track Scale 3; minimum fielded force 8,000 BV / 320 PV.
contract.bonus: Sandoval favor — a clean defense of Port Paix grants +1 Reputation and a standing invitation to the House Sandoval purchase table (heavier AFFS iron) in your next Draconis March contract.

a.blurb: Hold the March's throne world — anchor the highway into Port Paix, keep Combine 'Mechs off the Sandoval seat, then throw them off Robinson bloodied.
a.situation: The Combine has thrust in force at Port Paix — not to take Robinson, but to put its 'Mechs within sight of the Sandoval seat and shame the whole March. The militia is proud and stretched across a dozen approaches at once. Anchor the highway into the capital and hold the outer line while the regulars concentrate to answer.

b.employer: Draconis Combine — DCMS March-front command (the Robinson thrust)

contract.constraints: Command House (a DCMS liaison directs the thrust — this is a statement, and the Dragon wants it made correctly). Salvage Exchange (the Combine claims Davion wrecks; you take the cash).
contract.additionalRequirements: Track Scale 3; a heavy thrust force — you are meant to be SEEN at the gates of the March capital.
contract.bonus: Reach the seat — put a Combine 'Mech within sight of Port Paix's Sandoval hall (win Track 1) or win both tracks, and the DCMS pays a prestige bonus: +1 Reputation with the Combine and a Combine heavy-iron purchase offer next contract.

b.blurb: Fight for the Dragon — drive a thrust up the Port Paix highway and prove to the whole March that its heart can be reached.
b.situation: Robinson cannot be held, and holding it is not the mission. The Dragon means to be seen at the March capital's gates: drive the thrust up the Port Paix highway and put Combine iron within sight of the Sandoval hall. Every kilometer up that road is a sentence in the message the whole border will read.

hotspots.situation:
Robinson is the throne world of the Draconis March — the seat of House Sandoval, the family that has held this border against the Draconis Combine for centuries. It is not a rich world. The air is thin, the land is dry, and the population is small for a capital. What Robinson has is meaning: it is the place the whole March looks to, the ground the Sandovals have bled for since before anyone alive can remember. A world like New Ivaarsen is worth taking for its factories. Robinson is worth hurting for what hurting it says.

That is exactly what the Draconis Combine intends in the spring of 3151. Not an invasion — the Combine cannot hold the March capital and knows it — but a thrust in force at Port Paix, meant to put Combine 'Mechs within sight of the Sandoval seat and prove to the whole border that the March's heart can be reached. It is an insult delivered by regiment. The Robinson March Militia is proud, well-drilled, and stretched thin covering a dozen approaches at once, and its commanders would rather not gamble the capital on being in the right place at the right time.

So they hire you. Your command becomes the militia's swing force on the highway that runs into Port Paix: hold the outer line long enough for the regulars to concentrate against the thrust. Do that, and the militia will want to turn the tables — a counterstroke to throw the Combine off Robinson bloodied and embarrassed. Fail, and the fight collapses back onto the capital's own gates, where there is nowhere left to give ground. The March is watching either way.

contract.additionalRequirements: Track Scale 3; minimum fielded force 8,000 BV / 320 PV.
contract.bonus: Sandoval favor — a clean defense of Port Paix grants +1 Reputation and a standing invitation to the House Sandoval purchase table (heavier AFFS iron) in your next Draconis March contract.

missionBrief.behindScenes: The Combine thrust is a statement, not a conquest. Its commander pushes hard for the capital in Track 1 to be seen doing it; the Track 1 result decides whether you get to answer with a counterstroke (Assault) or fight a last-ditch stand at the gates (Pushback).

complications.effect: None.
Sandoval banner. A militia honor guard fights alongside you but must not be lost — a destroyed banner unit is -1 Reputation at contract end.
Press corps. The capital's cameras are rolling; any dishonorable act (firing on ejected pilots, ignoring a surrender) is -1 Reputation.
Dust storm. -1 to all ranged to-hit and no spotting beyond 6 hexes for the first 3 turns (thin air, arid dust).
Liaison commits. The Sandoval liaison pushes one of your units 3 hexes forward at setup.
Roll twice, ignore repeats.

missionBrief.contractVictory: Federated Suns: hold Port Paix's approaches (win Track 1) and then win the follow-up. Draconis Combine: reach the capital objective, or win both tracks.

namedCharacters.name: Chu-sa Rei Tanaka
namedCharacters.rule: Leads the thrust; fights to be seen, not to die. Withdraws his own unit if crippled. If killed, the Combine force is -2 Initiative for the rest of that track (Commander rule).

missionBrief.purchaseOptions: Between tracks, buy from a Sandoval March-Militia list — medium and heavy 'Mechs and combat vehicles, 2D6 of 7+. Assaults available only after a Track 1 win.

tracks.name: The Highway to Port Paix
tracks.situation:
The Combine thrust comes up the old highway that runs from the dry southern flats straight into Port Paix. There is one good junction where the road forks toward the capital's outer districts, and whoever owns that junction owns the pace of the whole battle. The militia is racing its main body to the fight from three directions at once; your command is the anchor that has to be standing on the junction when they arrive.

This is a holding action, not a duel. The Combine wants to blow through you fast, before the militia concentrates, so expect a hard frontal push with everything it has. You do not have to destroy the thrust — you have to be immovable long enough that arriving faster stops mattering. Every turn the junction stays in your hands is a turn the Sandovals get to bring another company to bear.
tracks.deployment: Short edges. You (Defender) hold one-third of your force off-map (arriving end of Turn 1, anywhere in your own half); the rest sets up within 6 hexes of your home edge (12" AS; 12/18" at Scale 2+). No Battlefield Support strikes — the capital's air-defense grid owns the sky. The Combine (Attacker) enters Turn 1.

objectives.text: Hold the Junction — half your force within 4 hexes of the highway junction at end of Turn 3 (6/12" Turn 4 at Scale 2+).
Overpower — more non-crippled BV/PV near the junction than the Combine at end of Turn 6 (Turn 8 AS at Scale 2+).
Cut Off the Head — destroy the Combine thrust's commander (Chu-sa Tanaka).

tracks.specialRules: The junction is the center hex for all objective checks. Voluntary withdrawal off your home edge counts as destroyed for objectives only.
tracks.trackEnd: End of Turn 6 (Turn 8 AS at Scale 2+).
tracks.salvagePolicy: Winner-all (SP at your salvage %).

forks.trigger: You held the junction; the thrust is spent and the militia has arrived in strength.
forks.consequence: Turn the tables — a counterstroke to run the Combine off Robinson with a bloody nose.

forks.trigger: The junction fell; the thrust is loose on the capital's outskirts.
forks.consequence: Fall back to the gates of Port Paix for a last-ditch stand.

tracks.name: Off Our Ground
tracks.situation:
The thrust shot its bolt at the junction and the militia is finally concentrated. Now the Sandovals want more than a hold — they want the Combine thrown off Robinson in front of the same cameras that watched it arrive. You lead the counterstroke into the Combine's staging ground on the southern flats, where its force is regrouping to withdraw.

This is your fight to force. The Combine commander would happily leave now with his statement made; your job is to make sure he leaves broken instead. Hit the staging ground before it can lift, break the back of the thrust, and the insult turns into a Sandoval victory the whole March will hear about.
tracks.deployment: Long edges. You (Attacker) enter Turn 1. The Combine (Defender) sets up within 5 hexes of its home edge (AS 10") before Initiative; no minefield or immobile Battlefield Support.

objectives.text: Press the Attack — engage the Combine in melee or fire for 2 consecutive turns.
Stand Fast — the Combine keeps its whole force on-map for 3 turns.
Conquer — reduce the Combine to half its starting BV/PV (tie = neither).
Hold the Field — leave no Combine 'Mech in play at track end.

tracks.trackEnd: Default (one side has no 'Mechs in play, or Turn 10 / Turn 8 AS).
tracks.salvagePolicy: Winner-all (SP at your salvage %).

forks.trigger: The counterstroke is decided; the Combine lifts, one way or another.
forks.consequence: Contract closes — settle Reputation and the Sandoval favor.

tracks.name: The Gates of Port Paix
tracks.situation:
The junction is gone and the Combine is in the capital's outer districts, close enough to the Sandoval seat that its guns can be heard from the palace steps. There is no more room to trade ground. You and what's left of the militia set up in the streets before the inner gate and hold it, because behind you is the one place on Robinson that cannot be allowed to fall.

The Combine does not have to take the palace — it only has to be seen at the gate. So it will come on hard and fast to get its footage and go. Your task is to deny it even that: hold the gate line, bleed the thrust in the narrow streets, and push it back out of the districts before it can plant a banner where the cameras will see. This is the ugly fight, close and desperate, and the whole point is that it never should have come to this.
tracks.deployment: Short edges. You (Defender) set up first, at least 5 hexes (10"; 10/16" at Scale 2+) off your own edge. The Combine (Attacker) gets +32 BSP per scale of vehicle assets and must split into two forces: force 1 enters its home edge Turn 1, force 2 from the long edges past midfield.

objectives.text: Hold the Gate — half your force in the district before the inner gate, engaged, for 2 consecutive turns.
Reach the Gate — half the Combine force crosses the center line toward the gate.
Advance to the Rear — push 75% of the Combine attackers back out of the districts by Turn 10.
Make Them Hurt — destroy or cripple half the Combine force.

tracks.specialRules: The inner gate is the center objective; a Combine unit that ends a turn adjacent to it while unopposed scores the Attacker's 'reach' order.
tracks.trackEnd: Default.
tracks.salvagePolicy: Pool-draft (wrecks pooled, alternate picks, winner first).

forks.trigger: The stand at the gate is over; the Combine has its footage or it doesn't.
forks.consequence: Contract closes — settle Reputation; a lost capital defense stings the March's pride and your name with it.

hotspots.title: The Four Cities Gambit
hotspots.employer: Draconis Combine — Tigress industrial keiretsu (DCMS liaison)

a.employer: Draconis Combine — Tigress industrial keiretsu (DCMS liaison)

contract.constraints: Salvage is generous — the keiretsu wants Suns wrecks studied and is happy to let you sell what you drag off the field. Command cannot be lowered below House (a DCMS liaison observes; the prototype is a state matter).
contract.additionalRequirements: Track Scale 2; minimum fielded force 5,000 BV / 200 PV.
contract.bonus: Prototype intact bonus — if the prototype hall is never breached across the contract, +1 Reputation with the Combine and a one-time offer of a piece of the new targeting hardware for your own use (a small permanent to-hit edge on one unit, GM-tracked).

a.blurb: Stand on the Combine's factory floor — keep the AFFS raiders out of the Four Cities prototype hall and make sure nothing valuable walks off Tigress.
a.situation: An AFFS raiding force is coming for the Four Cities, and the prototype targeting line — weeks from proving out — is what it wants. The regulars are committed elsewhere and the keiretsu will not gamble its plant on a thin garrison. Stand on the factory floor, keep the raiders out of the hall, and let nothing valuable leave Tigress.

b.employer: Federated Suns — AFFS deep-raiding command (the Four Cities prototype grab)

contract.constraints: Command Independent (a deep raid across the line — no liaison; officially the Suns were never on Tigress). Salvage 40% (a raider keeps a good share). Transport 50% (you make your own way in and out).
contract.additionalRequirements: Track Scale 2; a fast grab force — reach the hall, load the prototype, and run it off the field before the Combine can answer.
contract.bonus: Get the take home — breach the prototype hall and carry components off the field, and the AFFS pays a recovery bonus: +1 Reputation and a share of what the new hardware is worth to the Suns' own labs.

b.blurb: Raid the Dragon's jewel — punch into the Four Cities, seize the prototype targeting hardware, and be gone before the Combine can answer.
b.situation: The Combine's next-generation targeting hardware is weeks from proving out in a Four Cities hall, and the Suns want it on a lab bench, not a Kurita 'Mech. This is a deep raid across the line — no liaison, no flag, officially you were never on Tigress. Get in, load the prototype, and be gone before the Combine answers.

hotspots.situation:
Tigress is the Draconis Combine's industrial jewel on this stretch of the border — three billion people and an A-A rated manufacturing base spread across six landmasses, with the sprawl the locals simply call the Four Cities at its heart. Its lines turn out 'Mechs, munitions, and something the Combine guards more jealously than either: a prototype run of next-generation targeting hardware, only weeks from proving out. On a world this valuable the Combine keeps regulars, but regulars are busy pushing at the Federated Suns elsewhere in the Reach, and the keiretsu that owns the Four Cities does not trust its plant to a garrison spread thin.

The Federated Suns knows about the prototype line too. In the summer of 3151 an AFFS raiding force comes for it — not to hold Tigress, but to grab what it can from the Four Cities and be gone before the Combine can answer. The keiretsu, cutting through the usual channels, hires your command directly to stand on its factory floor and stop the grab. You fight for the Combine here, which means the enemy across the field flies Federated Suns colors and the honor rules cut the other way from the last time you took Draconis coin.

Your contract is narrow and the keiretsu means to keep it that way: keep the raiders out of the prototype hall, and if they get anything, make sure they don't get away with it. Do it clean and the Combine's memory is long and its purse deep. Let the prototype walk and you'll find no more work on this side of the line.

contract.constraints: Salvage is generous — the keiretsu wants Suns wrecks studied and is happy to let you sell what you drag off the field. Command cannot be lowered below House (a DCMS liaison observes; the prototype is a state matter).
contract.additionalRequirements: Track Scale 2; minimum fielded force 5,000 BV / 200 PV.
contract.bonus: Prototype intact bonus — if the prototype hall is never breached across the contract, +1 Reputation with the Combine and a one-time offer of a piece of the new targeting hardware for your own use (a small permanent to-hit edge on one unit, GM-tracked).

missionBrief.behindScenes: The AFFS raid is fast and greedy. It will go straight for the prototype hall in Track 1; the Track 1 result decides whether you chase down what escaped (Pursuit) or scramble to learn what was taken (Recon) before it reaches the Suns lines.

complications.effect: None.
Working plant. The Four Cities lines are still running; civilian workers fill the buildings — collateral in a factory hex is -1 Reputation at contract end.
Keiretsu security. A company of local security 'Mechs joins you but obeys the liaison, not you; the GM commits them.
Prototype telemetry. The first friendly unit within 3 hexes of the prototype hall each track gets +1 to-hit for that turn (the hardware helping its makers).
Monsoon. Heavy rain — +1 to all ranged to-hit and Piloting +1 on any run/jump for the first 4 turns (Tigress is 70% water and it shows).
Roll twice, ignore repeats.

missionBrief.contractVictory: Draconis Combine: the prototype hall is never breached, or you recover everything the raiders take. Federated Suns: breach the prototype hall AND get the take off-world (exit the Suns edge).
missionBrief.tally: Take Carried — each prototype component the raiders carry off the field counts 1. At 2+, the Combine considers the contract half-failed regardless of tracks won: no Reputation gain, and the prototype bonus is void.

namedCharacters.name: Leftenant Marisa Kell
namedCharacters.rule: Leads the grab; will break off with the take rather than trade blows. If her unit is destroyed while carrying a component, the component drops in that hex (recoverable).

missionBrief.purchaseOptions: Between tracks, buy from a DCMS supply list — medium/heavy 'Mechs and combat vehicles, 2D6 of 7+ (-1 per prototype component carried off). No Federated Suns designs (the Combine will not arm you with the enemy's iron).

tracks.name: The Prototype Hall
tracks.situation:
The raid drops onto the Four Cities and drives straight for the prototype hall — two hardened production buildings where the new targeting hardware sits half-assembled. The AFFS force does not want a fight; it wants the crates inside those buildings and a clear road to its DropShips. You are standing between the raiders and the most valuable thing on Tigress, and the whole battle is a race measured in what gets carried out the door.

The grab is the game here. The raiders will try to reach the hall, load components, and run them off their edge; you have to keep the hall sealed and punish anything that gets its hands on the take. Every crate that leaves the field is a Combine failure the keiretsu will remember, so this is not a fight you can win on kills alone — you win it by making sure the prototype stays where it belongs.
tracks.deployment: Short edges. You (Defender) set up all on-map, with half your force within 6 hexes of the two indestructible Medium prototype buildings placed within 4 hexes (6 at Scale 2+) of center. The Combine liaison's security may deploy with you. The AFFS (Attacker) enters Turn 1.

objectives.text: Guard the Hall — all your units stay within reach of the prototype buildings for the first 2 turns.
Reach the Hall — one raider unit per scale crosses the center toward the buildings.
You Must Pay for That — destroy raider units (100 VP per AFFS unit killed).
Grab the Stuff — carry prototype components off the AFFS edge (100 VP per component; each also adds to the Take Carried tally).

tracks.specialRules: Component-carry mini-game: carrying capacity by weight class (Light 1 / Medium 2 / Heavy 3 / Assault 4, or cargo/5t); a hand loads 1 component per turn; a carrying unit is -1 MP (AS -2") and a jump forces a Piloting check; infantry may load but never carry. A component in a destroyed carrier drops in that hex.
tracks.trackEnd: Turn 12 (AS Turn 10).
tracks.salvagePolicy: Attacker takes none; Defender-if-win, else units return to owners.

forks.trigger: You held the hall, but the surviving raiders are running for their DropShips with whatever they could grab.
forks.consequence: Run them down before they lift — every carrier stopped is a component saved.

forks.trigger: The raiders breached the hall and got clear with part of the prototype.
forks.consequence: Scramble to learn exactly what they took and where it's headed, before it reaches the Suns lines.

tracks.name: Run Them to the Ships
tracks.situation:
The raid is broken but not finished — small groups of AFFS 'Mechs are sprinting across the coastal lowlands toward their DropShips, and some of them are carrying pieces of the prototype. The keiretsu wants those pieces back and does not much care about the raiders otherwise. You chase, and the chase is everything: what you catch stays on Tigress, what you miss lifts for the Suns lines.

The raiders have a head start and lighter machines built to run, so you will not catch all of them. Pick your targets — the carriers first, the fast movers second — and cut off the road to the landing zone before the last of them slips past. Stop three-quarters of them short of the ships and the grab becomes a story about a raid that came all this way for nothing.
tracks.deployment: Short edges, same-edge start (both from the Combine home edge). The AFFS raiders (Defender/quarry) enter Turn 1, running for their DropShips — half their force must have a top move of 8 or less (their carriers and beaten stragglers; voluntary crits to qualify). You (Attacker/pursuer) enter Turn 2, chasing from the same edge.

objectives.text: Engage — engage at least half the AFFS units.
Break for the Ships — the AFFS get half their force by BV/PV across the center toward the far edge.
Prevention — stop 75% of the AFFS force from exiting the far edge by Turn 10.
No Quarter — destroy the entire AFFS force.

tracks.specialRules: A carrier stopped or destroyed before it exits drops its prototype component in-hex (recovered, removed from the Take Carried tally).
tracks.trackEnd: Turn 10 (or no non-crippled units on a side).
tracks.salvagePolicy: Attacker-only-if-win; else units return to owners.

forks.trigger: The last of the raid reaches its ships or dies short of them.
forks.consequence: Contract closes — tally the Take Carried and settle the Combine's favor.

tracks.name: What They Took
tracks.situation:
The prototype hall was breached and the raiders got clear with part of the new hardware. Now the keiretsu needs to know exactly what walked out the door — which components, in whose hands, headed where — before it reaches a Federated Suns lab and stops being a Combine secret. The raiders left a rear guard on the approach to their landing zone to buy the carriers time, and behind that screen is everything you need to learn.

This is a scouting fight, not a slugging match. Push scouts through the AFFS rear guard, read the withdrawing column, and identify what it's carrying and where it's bound. The rear guard will try to blind you and run out the clock; get eyes on two-thirds of it and the Combine can at least chase the theft off-world with couriers and warrants instead of guesswork.
tracks.deployment: You (Attacker/scout) pick any edge first; the AFFS rear guard (Defender) takes any other and sets up anywhere with at least half its force in the half nearest you. You enter Turn 1.

objectives.text: Scan the Column — scan (identify) one AFFS unit per scale.
Screen the Withdrawal — half the AFFS rear guard survives on-map for 2 turns.
Identify the Opposition — scan two-thirds of the AFFS force.
Preemptive Strike — destroy or cripple 25% of the AFFS rear guard.

tracks.specialRules: Scanning follows Recon rules. Identifying a carrier unit reveals which prototype component it holds (the keiretsu's whole aim here).
tracks.trackEnd: Turn 8.
tracks.salvagePolicy: None (scanning rules active).

forks.trigger: The column is read or it slips into the dark.
forks.consequence: Contract closes — the Combine settles up, and a prototype loose in Suns hands sours your standing whether you learned its name or not.

hotspots.title: Heat and Dust
hotspots.employer: Draconis Combine — Dahar IV district command (DCMS liaison)

a.employer: Draconis Combine — Dahar IV district command (DCMS liaison)

contract.constraints: Salvage is decent — the Combine wants any Suns machine you can drop and drag out of the sand. Command House (a DCMS liaison rides along).
contract.additionalRequirements: Track Scale 2; minimum fielded force 5,000 BV / 200 PV.
contract.bonus: Waypoint held — hold Bauxum and the Combine grants +1 Reputation and a free resupply (rearm + heal for your whole force) before your next contract.

a.blurb: Seize the water for the Combine — beat the Davion column to the Bauxum pan and own the approach to the whole northern desert for the season.
a.situation: Dahar is won at its waypoints, and Bauxum — a hardpan flat with the only water for a hundred kilometers — owns the northern desert this season. A Davion column is patrolling out of the border to take it. Reach the pan first and hold it, and mind the heat: this world kills machines before the enemy does.

b.employer: Federated Suns — AFFS border-patrol command (the Dahar dead-zone sweep)

contract.constraints: Salvage is decent — the March wants Combine iron pulled from the sand. Command House (an AFFS liaison rides the column).
contract.additionalRequirements: Track Scale 2; minimum fielded force 5,000 BV / 200 PV.
contract.bonus: Waypoint held — hold Bauxum and the March grants +1 Reputation and a free resupply (rearm + heal for your whole force) before your next contract.

b.blurb: Take the water for the Suns — race the Combine column to Bauxum and hold the only cache in a hundred kilometers of furnace.
b.situation: The Combine is moving a column on the Bauxum waypoint — water, landing ground, and the key to the whole northern desert. Whoever owns the pan operates out here; whoever loses it walks home. Beat them to it or take it off them, and watch your heat curves — at fifty-five degrees the desert fights both sides.

hotspots.situation:
Dahar IV is a furnace. A searing fifty-five degrees at the equator, a fifth of it water and the rest baked hardpan and dune, it sits on the Draconis Combine's side of the Reach line but close enough to the border that both Houses run patrols through its dead-zone deserts, testing each other's reach. The Combine holds it, but holding a desert is mostly a question of who owns the handful of waypoints — the water caches, the fuel dumps, the hardpan flats wide enough to set down a DropShip. Everything else out here is just distance and heat.

The Combine district command hires your mercenaries for exactly that kind of work: a recon-in-force to seize and hold the Bauxum waypoint — a rare flat with water — before a Federated Suns column patrolling out of the border does the same. Neither side has committed regiments to a rock this hot. It is a probing fight between two mobile columns that happen to want the same ground on the same day, and whoever owns Bauxum owns the approach to the whole northern desert for the season.

The catch is the heat itself. Machines run hot on Dahar IV before a shot is fired, water is life and the waypoint is the only water for a hundred kilometers, and a column that loses this clash does not just lose ground — it loses the ability to operate out here at all. This is a meeting engagement in the worst possible place to have one.

contract.constraints: Salvage is decent — the Combine wants any Suns machine you can drop and drag out of the sand. Command House (a DCMS liaison rides along).
contract.additionalRequirements: Track Scale 2; minimum fielded force 5,000 BV / 200 PV.
contract.bonus: Waypoint held — hold Bauxum and the Combine grants +1 Reputation and a free resupply (rearm + heal for your whole force) before your next contract.

missionBrief.behindScenes: A single sharp clash. Both columns want Bauxum and its water; the meeting engagement decides it in one track. Heat rules bite both sides equally.

complications.effect: None.
Mirage. Spotting beyond 8 hexes fails on a 1-2 (1D6) for the first 4 turns — the heat-shimmer hides everything.
Liaison commits. The DCMS liaison pushes one of your units 3 hexes forward at setup.
Sandstorm. +1 to all ranged to-hit for the first 3 turns.
Cracked coolant. One random friendly unit starts the track at +3 heat (a line burst in the drive out).
Roll twice, ignore repeats.

missionBrief.contractVictory: Whoever ends the track in control of Bauxum — more non-crippled BV/PV within 3 hexes of the water cache — wins the waypoint and the desert approach.

namedCharacters.name: Major Piet Roux
namedCharacters.rule: Leads the Suns column; fights hard for the water but withdraws his column if Bauxum is clearly lost — no one dies of thirst for a lost cache.

missionBrief.purchaseOptions: None mid-contract (a single track). Between contracts a Combine desert-warfare list opens — heat-efficient designs, 2D6 of 7+.

tracks.name: The Bauxum Pan
tracks.situation:
The two columns crest the dunes onto the Bauxum flat at almost the same moment — a wide hardpan pan with the water cache at its center, ringed by dune ridges that break line of sight. Neither side deployed for a fight; both were racing for the water and found the enemy already arriving. There is no time to maneuver into a good position and no good position to reach. You fight from where you stand.

The pan is the prize and the trap at once. Its center holds the water but offers no cover; its edges give cover but not the cache. Push for the center too early and you cook under crossfire on open hardpan; hold the ridges too long and the enemy drinks first and owns the ground. The heat makes every exchange costly — an alpha strike can shut a machine down out here — so this fight rewards the column that keeps its discipline in the oven a few turns longer than the other one does.
tracks.deployment: Short edges. Both columns enter their own home edge on Turn 1. Neither side may use minefield or immobile Battlefield Support — this is a meeting engagement, and nobody prepared the ground.

objectives.text: Close the Distance — engage, or approach within 12 hexes of the enemy, for 2 consecutive turns.
Make Their Acquaintance — be the FIRST to destroy one-third of the enemy by BV/PV (simultaneous = neither; units that withdraw early count as crippled).
Suppressing Fire — inflict at least one point of internal damage on every enemy unit.

tracks.specialRules: Bauxum heat: any unit that ends its Movement Phase on the open center hexes of the pan takes +1 heat that turn (the hardpan bakes). The water-cache hex, if held at track end (more non-crippled BV within 3 hexes), is the contract's waypoint-control result.
tracks.trackEnd: Default (one side has no 'Mechs in play, or Turn 10 / Turn 8 AS).
tracks.salvagePolicy: Winner-all (SP at your salvage %).

forks.trigger: The clash on the pan is decided.
forks.consequence: Contract closes — whoever holds Bauxum holds the northern desert for the season; settle the waypoint bonus.

hotspots.title: The Roussilon Belt
hotspots.employer: Corporate — the Languedoc agri-combine (board contract, deniable)

a.employer: Corporate — the Languedoc agri-combine (board contract, deniable)

contract.constraints: Command Independent — the board wants none of its own officers on a deniable job. Salvage generous — the board has no use for pirate wrecks and lets you keep the proceeds.
contract.additionalRequirements: Track Scale 2; minimum fielded force 5,000 BV / 200 PV.
contract.bonus: Complex intact — if the Roussilon processing lines are never destroyed, +1 Reputation and a standing retainer with the Languedoc Combine (a discount on your next corporate contract).

a.blurb: Take back the Roussilon complex for the Languedoc board — break the raiders' hold and hand the processing lines back intact, quietly, with no House and no court involved.
a.situation: Raiders flying a pirate flag hold the Roussilon processing complex, and the board does not much care who paid them — it cares about the harvest. Break their hold and hand the lines back intact before the season turns. No House, no court, no publicity: kill who you must, but a burned complex is worthless to everyone.

b.employer: Corporate — a rival agri-combine (deniable, via a hired raider band)

contract.constraints: Command Independent — the rival board keeps its distance; you hold the belt under a pirate flag of convenience. Salvage generous — grab what the plantation belt is worth on the way out.
contract.additionalRequirements: Track Scale 2; minimum fielded force 5,000 BV / 200 PV.
contract.bonus: Hold what you took — keep the Roussilon complex out of Languedoc hands through the contract, and the rival board pays a hold bonus: +1 Reputation and a cut of the season's harvest revenue.

b.blurb: Hold the Roussilon complex under the raider flag — keep the Languedoc board's guns off the lines you seized until the harvest is the rival's to sell.
b.situation: The Languedoc board lost the Roussilon complex fairly — as far as any court will ever prove. Your job is to keep it lost: hold the belt under the raider flag until the harvest is bought and sold elsewhere. The board's hired guns are coming for the lines, and the flag you do not fly is the one that pays you.

hotspots.situation:
Sun Prairie is a plantation world — hot, wet, and green, its four continents carpeted in the estates of a handful of agri-combines that between them feed a dozen neighboring systems. There is no House garrison worth the name; the combines police their own belts with private security, and the real power here is whichever board controls the most processing capacity. It is a quiet world, right up until it isn't.

Your employer is one of those boards — the Languedoc Combine, which has spent a generation building toward control of the continent's largest processing complex at Roussilon. In the wet season of 3151 that complex is seized out from under it. Officially the raiders are pirates, a band that drifted in from the Periphery and got lucky. Unofficially, everyone on the board knows a rival combine paid for the pirates, their machines, and the intelligence that let them walk straight in. The board cannot prove it and would not say it aloud if it could. What it can do is hire outside guns to take the complex back before the harvest — quietly, with no House and no court involved.

That is your contract: break the raiders' hold on the Roussilon complex and hand it back intact. The board does not much care how many pirates you kill, but it cares a great deal that the processing lines survive — a burned complex is worthless to everyone, and a rival that can point at your wreckage is worse than one that simply lost the fight. This is a corporate war fought in deniable clothes, and you are the deniable part.

contract.constraints: Command Independent — the board wants none of its own officers on a deniable job. Salvage generous — the board has no use for pirate wrecks and lets you keep the proceeds.
contract.additionalRequirements: Track Scale 2; minimum fielded force 5,000 BV / 200 PV.
contract.bonus: Complex intact — if the Roussilon processing lines are never destroyed, +1 Reputation and a standing retainer with the Languedoc Combine (a discount on your next corporate contract).

missionBrief.behindScenes: The pirates are a rival combine's proxies. Track 1 is the flanking assault to break their hold; its result decides whether you run down the survivors (Pursuit) or have to hold the retaken complex against a counter (Defend). The board's real fear is the complex burning — collateral is the tally.

complications.effect: None.
Company town. Plantation workers still live in the complex; any factory-hex collateral is -1 Reputation at contract end.
Bought locals. A squad of turned security 'Mechs joins the raiders — the GM adds one light unit to the OpFor.
Monsoon. +1 to all ranged to-hit and Piloting +1 on any run/jump for the first 4 turns (Sun Prairie is 72% water and it shows).
Rival's cameras. Someone is filming for the rival board; any dishonorable act is -1 Reputation.
Roll twice, ignore repeats.

missionBrief.contractVictory: Languedoc Combine: retake the Roussilon complex intact. Raiders (rival): hold the complex, or burn it to deny it to everyone.
missionBrief.tally: Lines Lost — each processing building destroyed counts 1. At 2+, the board considers the job failed regardless of tracks won: no Reputation, no retainer.

namedCharacters.name: 'Captain' Sabine Vos
namedCharacters.rule: A professional wearing pirate colors. If pushed to the wall she will torch a processing hall rather than lose it — a standing burn threat the board is paying you to prevent.

missionBrief.purchaseOptions: Between tracks, a corporate grey-market list — medium/heavy 'Mechs + combat vehicles, 2D6 of 7+, no questions asked (the board pays).

tracks.name: Around the Roads
tracks.situation:
The raiders hold the Roussilon complex and its approaches, dug in among the processing halls with their heavy machines covering the obvious roads in. A frontal push up those roads would be a slaughter, and it would likely see the complex burned in the fighting — exactly what the board is paying you to prevent. So you do not come up the roads. You come around them.

The plan is a flank: pin the raiders' attention on the main approach with part of your force while the rest swings wide through the cane belts and hits the complex from a direction they never fortified. Get inside their perimeter before they can react and their careful defense becomes a trap they are standing in. The cane is high and wet and blocks line of sight both ways — which cuts as much for them as for you — but it is the only road to a clean retaking.
tracks.deployment: Long edges. The raiders (Defender) set up their whole force in their own half before Turn 1, plus two veteran Medium emplacements per scale dug into YOUR half (gun positions covering the roads; a no-BSP variant uses 30-CF bunkers). Your force (Attacker): one-third enters your home edge Turn 1, the rest sweeps in from a SHORT edge on Turn 2 — the flank through the cane.

objectives.text: Get Inside — get half your force into the raiders' half in any end phase.
Hold the Roads — the raiders keep half their force engaged on the main approach for 2 turns.
Crush the Hold — reduce the raiders to half their starting BV/PV.
Ramming Speed — destroy every raider emplacement.

tracks.specialRules: The Roussilon processing halls are Medium buildings across the raiders' half; a destroyed hall adds to Lines Lost. If the raiders are losing, Captain Vos may move to fire a hall herself (the burn threat) — GM discretion.
tracks.trackEnd: Turn 8 (AS 6).
tracks.salvagePolicy: None (Flank template — no wrecks claimed here; your salvage % applies on other tracks).

forks.trigger: The flank broke the raiders' hold; Vos is pulling her survivors out toward the coast.
forks.consequence: Run them down before they reach their ships — a band that escapes clean comes back next season.

forks.trigger: The flank stalled; the raiders still hold part of the complex and now know you're here in force.
forks.consequence: Hold the ground you took against their counter-attack, in among the halls you can't afford to break.

tracks.name: Run Them to the Coast
tracks.situation:
The flank worked; the raiders' hold is broken and Captain Vos is pulling her survivors out of the Roussilon belt toward wherever her DropShips lie hidden in the coastal marsh. The board would be content just to have its complex back, but a pirate band that gets away clean is a band that returns next season — and the rival who paid them learns that hiring proxies works. Running them down sends a different message.

The raiders are fleeing through the wet lowlands where their lighter machines have the edge, so you will not catch all of them. Cut the marsh road, catch Vos's carriers and command units before they reach the coast, and the rival's whole investment turns into a total loss instead of a temporary setback. Let too many slip past and the season's quiet ends the same way it began.
tracks.deployment: Short edges, same-edge start (both from your home edge). The raiders (Defender/quarry) enter Turn 1, fleeing for the far edge — half their force must have a top move of 8 or less (their beaten stragglers; voluntary crits to qualify). You (Attacker/pursuer) enter Turn 2, chasing from the same edge.

objectives.text: Engage — engage at least half the raider units.
Break for the Coast — the raiders get half their force by BV/PV across the center toward their ships.
Prevention — stop 75% of the raiders from exiting the far edge by Turn 10.
No Quarter — destroy the entire raider band.

tracks.specialRules: Captain Vos, if still alive, runs — she will not turn to fight; catching her unit is worth the contract's message to the rival board.
tracks.trackEnd: Turn 10 (or no non-crippled units on a side).
tracks.salvagePolicy: Attacker-only-if-win, else units return to owners (Pursuit template).

forks.trigger: The raiders reach the coast or die in the marsh.
forks.consequence: Contract closes — settle the complex-intact bonus and the board's retainer.

tracks.name: Hold What You Took
tracks.situation:
The flank did not break them cleanly. The raiders still hold part of the Roussilon complex, and now they know you are here in force. Captain Vos does the professional thing: she consolidates on the processing halls and dares you to dig her out, knowing the board will not let you level the place to do it. You have taken ground, but you have not taken the complex, and until you hold all of it the job is not done.

The raiders counter-attack to retake what you gained, and you have to hold the line you pushed to — in among the halls, where every exchange risks the fire the board is paying you to prevent. This is the ugly middle of a corporate war: close, careful fighting over machinery neither side is allowed to break, decided by who can hold their nerve and their aim in the narrow lanes between the processing lines.

Cut Off the Head — destroy Captain Vos's unit.

The regulars have failed to break it twice. Open the road before the Suns' reinforcements turn the tide, and the whole landing floods inland toward Last Chance.

b.blurb: Hold the Weller neck for the Suns — keep the road bottled and the Combine landing trapped on the beaches until the tide runs out on them.

The line between the sea and the bluffs has already thrown back two assaults. Hold it one more time, against whatever the Combine sends to open it, until the tide of reinforcements turns for good.

hotspots.situation:
Melcher is a water world with just enough land to fight over — three continents scattered across a temperate ocean, its cities strung along coasts and river mouths, its wealth in shipping and the fisheries that feed half the district. It sits astride a Reach shipping lane the Draconis Combine wants and the Federated Suns holds, and in the ilClan era's grinding border war it has changed hands twice without either side quite keeping it.

In 3151 the Combine comes for it again, and this time the plan hinges on the Weller coast — a narrow neck of land where the only road inland runs between the sea and a range of bluffs. A Federated Suns blocking force has dug in across that neck, and as long as it holds, the Combine's landing at Weller is bottled up on the beaches. The Combine command hires your mercenaries to do what its own regulars have failed to do twice: break the Suns line on the Weller neck and open the road inland.

This is a breakthrough in the hardest place to make one — a coastal chokepoint where the Suns have every advantage of ground and you have to go through them, not around. Break the line and the Combine landing floods inland toward Last Chance; fail, and the beachhead becomes a trap the Suns close at their leisure. The Combine does not care how you open the road, only that it opens before the tide of Suns reinforcements turns against the landing.

contract.bonus: Road opened — break the Weller line and the Combine grants +1 Reputation and priority resupply (rearm + heal) before your next contract.

missionBrief.behindScenes: A breakthrough at a coastal chokepoint. Track 1 is the assault on the Weller neck; SUCCESS opens the exploitation inland (t2a), FAILURE strands you defending the beachhead (t2b).

complications.effect: None.
High tide. The seaward hex rows become Level 1 water for 3 turns — Piloting checks to move through them.
Naval fire support. One friendly Battlefield Support artillery strike is free this track (the landing fleet's guns).
Sea fog. Spotting beyond 6 hexes fails on a 1-2 (1D6) for the first 3 turns.
Liaison commits. The DCMS liaison pushes one of your units 3 hexes forward at setup.
Roll twice, ignore repeats.

missionBrief.contractVictory: Draconis Combine: break the Weller line (win Track 1) and win the exploitation. Federated Suns: hold the neck.

namedCharacters.name: Leftenant Colonel Dana Verhoeven
namedCharacters.rule: Holds the Weller line; a stubborn defender who fights to the last bluff. If killed, the Suns force is -2 Initiative for the rest of that track (Commander rule).

missionBrief.purchaseOptions: Between tracks, a Combine amphibious-assault list — jump-capable and waterproofed designs, medium/heavy, 2D6 of 7+.

tracks.name: The Weller Neck
tracks.situation:
The Weller neck is a kilometer of open road between the surf and the bluffs, and the Federated Suns own both ends of it. Their line is anchored on the high ground with the sea guarding one flank, so there is no clever approach — the road is the road, and the Suns have ranged every meter of it. Your force comes off the beaches and up the neck into the teeth of a prepared defense, because behind you the whole Combine landing is waiting on you to open the way.

A breakthrough is not a brawl; it is a race against the clock. You do not have to destroy the Suns line — you have to get enough of your force past it and onto the inland road before the defense can seal the gap. Punch through, push your spearhead off the far edge, and the neck is broken. Get bogged down trading fire on the open road and the tide, literal and figurative, runs out on you.
tracks.deployment: Long edges. The Federated Suns (Defender) sets up within 6 hexes of its home edge (12" AS); you (Attacker) enter Turn 1.

objectives.text: Cross the Neck — get half your force by BV/PV across the center line.
Hold the Road — the Suns keep half their force engaged for 2 consecutive turns.
Push Through — exit half your force off the Suns home edge onto the inland road.
Suppressing Fire — inflict at least one point of internal damage on every Suns unit.

tracks.specialRules: The seaward hex row is Level 1 water (the surf); the landward bluff hexes are Level 2 (the Suns high ground). Units exiting the Suns home edge are the breakthrough's spearhead.
tracks.trackEnd: Default (one side has no 'Mechs in play, or Turn 10 / Turn 8 AS).
tracks.salvagePolicy: Pool-draft (wrecks pooled, alternate picks, winner first).

forks.trigger: The Weller line is broken; the landing is pouring inland behind your spearhead.
forks.consequence: Drive on Last Chance before the Suns can form a second line.

forks.trigger: The line held; your force is pinned on the Weller beaches with the sea at its back.
forks.consequence: Hold the beachhead against the Suns counter-attack, or the landing dies on the sand.

tracks.name: Flood Inland
tracks.situation:
The Weller line is broken and the Combine landing is pouring inland behind you. The road to Last Chance is open, but the Federated Suns have not given up — they have pulled back to the town's outer districts and mean to make you fight for every block. You lead the spearhead into that fight, because momentum is everything now: hit the Suns before they can dig in, and the whole coast falls; give them a day, and it becomes a siege.

This is the assault the breakthrough was for. You come at the Suns holding position hard and fast, aiming to break their line and their will before reinforcements from deeper inland can reach them. Take the field and Melcher's coast belongs to the Combine; stall out, and you have traded a broken beachhead for a broken spearhead.
tracks.deployment: Long edges. The Suns (Defender) sets up within 5 hexes of its home edge (AS 10") before Initiative; no minefield or immobile Battlefield Support. You (Attacker) enter Turn 1.

objectives.text: Press the Attack — engage the Suns for 2 consecutive turns.
Stand Fast — the Suns keep their whole force on-map for 3 turns.
Conquer — reduce the Suns to half their starting BV/PV (tie = neither).
Hold the Field — leave no Suns 'Mech in play at track end.

tracks.trackEnd: Default.
tracks.salvagePolicy: Winner-all (SP at your salvage %).

forks.trigger: The drive on Last Chance is decided.
forks.consequence: Contract closes — settle the road-opened bonus and the Combine's favor.

tracks.name: Hold the Beach
tracks.situation:
The Weller line held, and now your force is pinned on the Weller beaches with the sea at its back and the Federated Suns counter-attacking to throw the whole landing back into it. The breakthrough failed; the job now is simply to survive — hold the beachhead long enough for the Combine to decide whether to reinforce or evacuate, because a landing overrun on the sand is the kind of disaster that ends careers.

The Suns smell blood and come on hard, trying to collapse the perimeter before the tide and the daylight both turn. You hold the line at the surf, trading ground you cannot afford to lose for the time the Combine needs, and hope the guns of the landing fleet and your own discipline are enough to keep the beachhead from becoming a grave.
tracks.deployment: Short edges. You (Defender) hold one-third of your force off-map (arriving end of Turn 1, own half); the rest sets up within 6 hexes of your home edge (12" AS; 12/18" at Scale 2+). The Suns (Attacker) enter Turn 1.

objectives.text: Hold the Beachhead — half your force within 4 hexes of the beachhead center at end of Turn 3 (6/12" Turn 4 at Scale 2+).
Overpower — more non-crippled BV/PV near the beachhead than the Suns at end of Turn 6 (Turn 8 AS at Scale 2+).
Cut Off the Head — destroy the Suns commander (Verhoeven).

tracks.trackEnd: End of Turn 6 (Turn 8 AS at Scale 2+).
tracks.salvagePolicy: Winner-all (SP at your salvage %).

forks.trigger: The beachhead holds, or it is overrun.
forks.consequence: Contract closes — a failed landing costs the Combine's favor and your standing.

b.blurb: Drive into Neu Sitten under Sho-sa Ishida — reach the government district for the cameras and be gone before a Suns relief column can cross the border.

The city is a stone maze built for the crush of 1.12 gravities. Fight it street by street, reach the capitol, and be out before any relief crosses the border.

hotspots.situation:
Lucerne is a high-gravity world of dry uplands and walled cities, its capital Neu Sitten a dense old town of narrow streets and close-packed towers built for the crush of 1.12 gravities. It answers to the Federated Suns on paper, but out here on the Reach border the House's attention is thin, and in practice Lucerne is run by its own planetary government — a proud, prickly, chronically underfunded administration that guards its autonomy as fiercely as its purse.

In the wet-season dark of 3151 a Draconis Combine raiding force lands near Neu Sitten and pushes into the city itself, aiming to seize the government district, embarrass the Suns, and be gone before a relief column can cross the border. The planetary militia is brave and outmatched, and the government will not wait weeks for House regulars who may never come. It hires what it can afford — your command — to push the raiders back out of Neu Sitten before they reach the capitol.

This is a knife-fight in a stone maze. The Combine is loose in the streets and pressing toward the government district; you have to shove them back out block by block, in a city where the buildings are cover for both sides and every collapse buries civilians the government answers to. The budget is thin and the politics are thick, but the job is simple: get the raiders out of Neu Sitten, and try not to level the place doing it.

contract.constraints: Command House (a militia liaison). Lower pay and thin support — the planetary purse is small and the government knows it.
contract.additionalRequirements: Track Scale 2; minimum fielded force 5,000 BV / 200 PV.
contract.bonus: Capitol saved — push the raiders out with the government district intact and the planetary government grants +1 Reputation and a standing local retainer (steady, low-paying garrison work whenever you pass through Lucerne).

missionBrief.behindScenes: A single urban Pushback. The Combine raiders are loose in Neu Sitten; push them back out before they reach the capitol. Collateral in the old town is the tally.

Crowded streets. Civilians still fill the government district; any building-hex collateral there is -1 Reputation at contract end.
Militia support. A lance of local militia 'Mechs joins you, but the liaison commits them, not you.
Night in the maze. Night rules and spotting beyond 5 hexes fails on a 1-2 (1D6) for the first 4 turns.
Barricades. The militia has thrown up rubble barricades — two Level 1 rough-terrain lines of the GM's placement in your half.
Roll twice, ignore repeats.

missionBrief.contractVictory: Planetary government: push 75% of the raiders back out of the city (across the center) before they reach the government district. Draconis Combine: reach the government district (map center).
missionBrief.tally: Old Town Damage — each city building destroyed in the government district counts 1. At 3+: -1 Reputation, and the standing local retainer is void.

namedCharacters.name: Sho-sa Ken Ishida
namedCharacters.rule: Leads the raid into the city; he will pull out if pushed hard, but he wants footage at the capitol first. If killed, the raiders are -2 Initiative for the rest of the track (Commander rule).

tracks.name: Block by Block
tracks.situation:
The Combine raiders have fought their way into Neu Sitten's western districts and are pushing east toward the government quarter through streets built for people, not 'Mechs. You come in behind and beside them, into a city where line of sight ends at the next corner and a heavy 'Mech is as much a prisoner of the streets as a master of them. The militia holds what it can of the eastern quarter; your job is to shove the raiders back the way they came.

A pushback in a city is a grind measured in blocks. You have to force the raiders back across the center of the map and out of the districts they have taken, while they try to bull through you toward the capitol. Buildings are cover, chokepoint, and casualty all at once — every hall you drop might be a raider's cover or a district full of the people the government sent you to protect. Push them out clean and Neu Sitten remembers you; wreck the old town doing it and the thin-lipped government finds a reason not to pay.
tracks.deployment: Short edges. You (Defender) set up first, at least 5 hexes (10"; 10/16" at Scale 2+) off your own edge. The Combine raiders (Attacker) get +32 BSP per scale of vehicle assets and must split into two forces: force 1 enters its home edge Turn 1, force 2 from the long edges past midfield.

objectives.text: Hold the Quarter — half your force engaged in the government-quarter approaches for 2 consecutive turns.
Reach the Capitol — half the Combine force crosses the center toward the government district.
Advance to the Rear — push 75% of the Combine raiders back across the center and out of the districts by Turn 10.
Make Them Hurt — destroy or cripple half the Combine force.

a.situation: A Combine salvage column is crawling the Eridanus wreck field, chaining down half-built Suns hulls for the hundred-day haul to the jump point. The Broadswords are pinned holding the capital and are subcontracting the chase, merc to merc. Run the column down on the open flats and clear the field — the salvage split is the real pay.

b.employer: Draconis Combine — DCMS salvage command (Chu-i Hana Ishikawa's recovery column)

contract.constraints: Salvage nonnegotiable-high — the whole job is lifting Suns hulls off the flats; the column keeps what it hauls to the black. Command Liaison (a DCMS salvage coordinator rides the column).
contract.additionalRequirements: Track Scale 2; minimum fielded force 5,000 BV / 200 PV. A fast screen is strongly advised — this is a running fight.

b.blurb: Get the looted Suns hulls off Achernar for the Dragon — keep the recovery column rolling to the jump point while a merc pursuer tries to pin you on the open flats.
b.situation: Chu-i Ishikawa's recovery column carries the prize the raid itself never won: the best hulls off the Eridanus field, cut free and chained for the long haul. A hundred days of open ground lie between her haulers and the black, and a merc pursuit is already saddling. Screen the column, keep it rolling, and get the iron to the jump point.

hotspots.situation:
Achernar burns bright — a blue-white giant so fierce it lends the world its name, and so far out that the jump point sits a hundred days' sail from the planet. What the light and the distance protect is worth protecting: an advanced industrial world (B-A-B-B-A) whose Eridanus works stamp out 'Mechs for the Federated Suns' border regiments. Iron leaves Achernar; the Draconis March spends it holding everything east of here.

A week ago a Combine raid came for those works and was thrown back hard, leaving the Eridanus flats studded with wreckage — dead machines from both sides, and among them a run of half-built line 'Mechs the raiders never reached. The raiders did not leave empty-handed, though. A Combine salvage column stayed behind in the confusion, and it is now crawling the wreck field with recovery haulers, cutting free the best hulls and chaining them down for the long haul to the jump point. A hundred days of open ground lies between that column and the black — but only if it keeps rolling.

The AFFS garrison here is Hale's Broadswords, a heavy mercenary regiment, and they are pinned holding the capital approaches on Agnetenar with nothing fast to spare. So their commander, Colonel Reigs Hale, does what mercenaries do and subcontracts the chase to you — merc to merc, a handshake and a cut. The money is a working wage, not a House purse, but the salvage split is generous: the Broadswords want the field cleared and their finder's fee, not the wrecks. Run the column down before it reaches the jump point and Achernar's iron rides home in your holds. Let it go, and a Combine analyst gets a crate of Suns hardware to take apart.

contract.additionalRequirements: Track Scale 2; minimum fielded force 5,000 BV / 200 PV. A fast element is strongly advised — this is a chase.
contract.bonus: Clear the field — recover the wreck field intact and the Broadswords add +1 Reputation with the mercenary trade and a shot at a salvaged 'Mech (one roll on their recovery table) before your next contract.

missionBrief.behindScenes: A salvage race across open ground. Track 1 is the pursuit; the Track 1 result drives the branch. SUCCESS pins the column into a laager for an Objective Raid (t2a); FAILURE lets it reach its DropShip screen for a Meeting Engagement (t2b). Both converge on holding the field (t3) while the Broadswords' techs strip it.

complications.effect: None.
Recovery hauler bogs. One Combine salvage hauler throws a tread and starts the track immobile mid-field — a fat target, and a prize.
The subcontractor's cut. Hale's Broadswords claim first pick of one recovered hull at contract end (-1 to your recovery-table roll).
Dust off the flats. Spotting beyond 8 hexes fails on a 1-2 (1D6) for the first 3 turns.
Bright-star glare. Units firing toward the primary (the eastern map edge) take -1 to-hit for the first 3 turns.
Roll twice, ignore repeats.

missionBrief.contractVictory: You: recover the wreck field — win the pursuit and hold the field in Track 3. Draconis Combine: exit half its salvage haulers toward the jump-point edge across the contract.
missionBrief.tally: Hulls Lifted — each Combine salvage hauler that exits toward the jump point counts 1. At 3+, the best 'Mechs are gone: -1 to your recovery-table roll and no +1 Reputation even on a win.

namedCharacters.name: Chu-i Hana Ishikawa
namedCharacters.rule: Runs the recovery column and fights a fast delaying action, trading ground for time. If killed, the Combine screen is -2 Initiative for the rest of that track (Commander rule).

missionBrief.purchaseOptions: Between tracks, a merc-market field list — light/medium 'Mechs and combat vehicles from the Broadswords' own spares, 2D6 of 7+. A recovered hull may be offered for internal sale.

tracks.name: Across the Eridanus Flats
tracks.situation:
The Combine salvage column is strung out across the open Eridanus flats, recovery haulers riding low under looted hulls, a light 'Mech screen shielding them. A hundred days of ground lies between them and the jump point, and the whole of it means nothing if you catch them here. You come onto the flats behind them, running.

A pursuit is about pinning, not just chasing. Force the column to turn and fight and the haulers stop — every turn they are stationary is a turn your employer's techs get closer to the field. Get past the screen and the slow, laden haulers are yours. Let that screen fight a clean delaying action and the column bleeds out the far edge with the best of Achernar's iron aboard.
tracks.deployment: Long edges. The Combine salvage column (Defender/quarry) enters its home edge on Turn 1 and must move toward the far, jump-point edge; its recovery haulers are laden and move at half speed. You (Attacker/pursuer) enter from the same home edge on Turn 2 at full speed. No Battlefield Support this track — a chase outruns the guns.

objectives.text: Run Them Down — engage or scan half the Combine column by end of Turn 4.
Stay Ahead — keep half your haulers moving toward the jump-point edge for 3 consecutive turns.
No Quarter — destroy or cripple half the column before it exits.
Break Contact — exit half the column (by count) off the jump-point edge.
First Blood — first side to destroy 25% of the enemy scores it; simultaneous = both score.

tracks.specialRules: Recovery haulers are the column's slow half and move at half speed. A hauler that exits the jump-point edge adds to Hulls Lifted.
tracks.trackEnd: Turn 10 (Turn 8 AS), or the column has no haulers left on-map.
tracks.salvagePolicy: Pool-draft on the pursuit's kills (wrecks pooled, alternate picks, winner first); the wreck field itself is settled in Track 3.

forks.trigger: You pinned the column; it has circled its haulers into a laager to fight you off.
forks.consequence: Raid the laager and take the recovered hulls before they can torch them.

forks.trigger: The column reached its DropShip screen; now it is a stand-up fight for the field.
forks.consequence: Meet the Combine relief in the open — whoever holds the flats holds the salvage.

tracks.name: The Laager on the Flats
tracks.situation:
The column could not outrun you, so it has circled — recovery haulers ringed by the light screen, the looted hulls chained down inside, torch charges rigged in case they cannot keep them. You have to get in fast: past the screen, into the laager, and stop them wrecking what they cannot carry.

An objective raid is a smash-and-grab, not a battle of attrition. Reach the marked haulers, secure them or kill their charges, and pull back before the Combine can make the field a bonfire. Every hull you tag is a hull your employer's techs recover whole; every one you leave burns to slag on the flats.
tracks.deployment: Long edges. The Combine (Defender) sets up within 6 hexes of center around three laagered haulers (Heavy vehicles / objective markers). You (Attacker) enter Turn 1.

objectives.text: Reach the Laager — get a unit adjacent to a marked hauler.
Torch It — destroy a marked hauler (deny the hull) before the raiders secure it.
Secure the Hulls — control (adjacent, no enemy adjacent) 2 of the 3 marked haulers at end of Turn 5.
Scorched Earth — destroy 2 of the 3 marked haulers.
Bloody the Screen — destroy or cripple half the enemy 'Mech screen.

tracks.specialRules: A marked hauler secured intact becomes a recovered hull (removed from Hulls Lifted risk). A hauler destroyed by either side is lost salvage.
tracks.trackEnd: End of Turn 8, or all marked haulers resolved.
tracks.salvagePolicy: Secured haulers feed the wreck-field pool (settled in Track 3 at your salvage %); pool-draft on the rest.

forks.trigger: The laager is settled, one way or the other.
forks.consequence: The Combine mounts one last push to burn the field before your techs finish.

tracks.name: The DropShip Guard
tracks.situation:
The column made its DropShip screen before you could pin it, and now the Combine has turned to fight for the field on even terms. Two forces come onto the Eridanus flats from opposite edges, neither dug in, both wanting the same ground — the wreck field lying between them.

A meeting engagement is decided by who seizes the center first and holds it. Get your weight onto the field and break the Combine line before it can consolidate around the haulers, and the salvage is yours to hold. Come in piecemeal and you will be the one pushed off Achernar's iron.
tracks.deployment: Short edges. Both forces enter Turn 1 from opposite home edges; neither sets up in advance. The wreck field is the center third of the map.

objectives.text: Seize the Center — more of your non-crippled BV/PV in the center third than the enemy at end of Turn 4.
Hold the Field — the same at end of Turn 8.
Break Them — reduce the enemy to half its starting BV/PV (tie = neither).
Commander's Fall — destroy the enemy commander's unit.

tracks.specialRules: Holding the center third at track end means your techs work the field first — an advantage carried into Track 3.
tracks.trackEnd: Default (Turn 10 / Turn 8 AS, or one side has no 'Mechs in play).
tracks.salvagePolicy: Winner-all on the field's pooled wrecks (paid as SP at your salvage %).

forks.trigger: The stand-up fight is decided.
forks.consequence: The Combine mounts one last push to burn the field before your techs finish.

tracks.name: Hold the Field
tracks.situation:
The chase is over and the wreck field is yours — for now. The Broadswords' recovery techs are already on the flats, cutting the best hulls free of the wreckage, and the job's last act is the simplest and the hardest: keep the Combine off them until the work is done. Whatever the Combine could not carry, it would rather burn than leave to you.

A last Combine push comes for the field — a spoiling attack to wreck what its salvagers could not lift. You hold a perimeter around the working techs, trading the open flats for the time they need. Hold, and Achernar's iron rides home in your holds; break, and the field goes up in smoke with your bonus in it.
tracks.deployment: Short edges. You (Defender) hold one-third of your force off-map (arriving end of Turn 1, own half); the rest sets up within 6 hexes of your home edge (12" AS; 12/18" at Scale 2+), the recovery techs (immobile objective markers) at center. The Combine (Attacker) enters Turn 1. Battlefield Support allowed — the Broadswords lend a flight.

objectives.text: Hold the Field — half your force within 4 hexes of the recovery site at end of Turn 3 (6/12" Turn 4 at Scale 2+).
Cover the Techs — no recovery marker destroyed through end of Turn 6.
Burn It Down — destroy half the recovery markers.
Overpower — more non-crippled BV/PV near the site than the enemy at track end.

tracks.specialRules: Each recovery marker destroyed adds to Hulls Lifted (the Combine burns what it cannot take). At contract close, apply Hulls Lifted: 3+ means -1 to your recovery-table roll and no +1 Reputation; the field held intact means +1 Reputation and a shot at a salvaged 'Mech.
tracks.trackEnd: End of Turn 6 (Turn 8 AS at Scale 2+).
tracks.salvagePolicy: Winner-all on the recovered field (your salvage %; the Broadswords keep their 20% finder's fee off the top).

forks.trigger: The field is held, or it is ash.
forks.consequence: Contract closes — tally Hulls Lifted and settle the Broadswords' finder's fee and your recovery-table roll.

hotspots.title: Gardena Blockade
hotspots.employer: Noble house — Baroness Ilse Adaire, landholder of Gardena (Draconis March)

The Baroness is buying a surgeon's cut, not a war: break the laager that feeds the blockade and let the strongpoints wither. Wreck her roads and workshops in the doing and the purse closes.

b.employer: Draconis Combine — deniable raiding command (Tai-i Nils Sasaki's cordon, no banner)
