b.blurb: Hold the deniable cordon around Gardena — keep the Orji laager feeding the strongpoints and strangle the estate's trade while the Baroness's hired guns come for your throat.
b.situation: The cordon on Gardena wears no banner and never will; what it does is squeeze. Keep the Orji laager feeding the road strongpoints and the estate's trade dies quietly, workshop by workshop. The Baroness has hired guns to come for the laager — hold the flats and the strangle holds itself.

hotspots.situation:
Alta Vista lies under a dim red-dwarf sun, an arid world of two dusty continents where the water is scarce and the wealth is in workshops. Around the capital, Gardena, a knot of advanced fabricators (the world rates A for tech) turns out precision parts the Draconis March cannot easily source elsewhere. House Adaire has held the landgrant for three generations, and Baroness Ilse Adaire runs it the way her grandmother did: quietly, profitably, and without asking New Avalon for much of anything.

That independence is being tested. A raider force — light armor and 'Mechs, well drilled, flying no flag anyone can prove — has thrown a loose blockade around Gardena. There are strongpoints on the three roads into the capital, a supply laager out on the Orji flats keeping them fed, and a slow strangle tightening on the city's trade. Everything about it is deniable: no declaration, no Combine banner, just professional soldiers with Combine-pattern machines who appeared the week the border went quiet. The AFFS will not divert a regiment for a landhold's private trouble it cannot officially blame on anyone.

So the Baroness hires you from her own purse, and she is precise about what she is buying. She wants the blockade's back broken, not a grinding battle that levels her own roads and workshops. Command is her whim, not a liaison's doctrine; the wrecks fall on Adaire land and she considers them estate property. Break the blockade where it is weakest — the Orji laager that feeds it — and the strongpoints wither on their own. Reputation here is with the March nobility, a small and long-memoried circle that hires on a word.

contract.constraints: Salvage capped low (Exchange) — wrecks fall on Adaire land and the estate claims them; you take the cash equivalent. Command House — the Baroness or her steward can commit you.
contract.additionalRequirements: Track Scale 2; minimum fielded force 4,000 BV / 160 PV.
contract.bonus: Break the blockade cleanly (Gardena's roads intact) and Baroness Adaire adds +1 Reputation with the March nobility and a retainer's purse (500 SP) at contract end. Wreck her roads and the purse is withheld.

missionBrief.behindScenes: A blockade-break in two tracks. Track 1 is the Strike on the Orji supply laager, the cordon's logistics heart; the Track 1 result drives the branch. SUCCESS starves the strongpoints and the raiders mass to retake the laager (t2a, Defend). FAILURE strands your strike force deep in raider ground (t2b, Breakthrough back out). The tree ends after Track 2.

complications.effect: None.
The Baroness is watching. A house observer rides with you; any collateral damage to a Gardena road hex is a -1 Reputation flag at contract end (she is counting).
Estate levy. One of the Baroness's own militia lances (two light 'Mechs, or a vehicle element) joins you — green (Gunnery 5 / Piloting 6), at her insistence.
Red-dwarf gloom. Alta Vista's dim primary — treat the first 2 turns as dusk (-1 to spotting beyond 10 hexes).
Steward's override. The Baroness's steward commits one of your units 3 hexes forward at setup, toward her priority, not yours.
Roll twice, ignore repeats.

missionBrief.contractVictory: You: break the blockade — take the laager in Track 1 and hold it (or escape clean) in Track 2. Draconis Combine (deniable): keep the laager, or force your strike force off the field.
missionBrief.tally: Roads Wrecked — each Gardena road hex destroyed (by anyone) counts 1. At 3+, the Baroness sours: -1 Reputation and the retainer's purse withheld.

namedCharacters.name: Tai-i Nils Sasaki
namedCharacters.rule: Runs the cordon from the Orji laager; a careful officer who fights for position over glory. If killed, the raiders are -2 Initiative for the rest of that track (Commander rule).

missionBrief.purchaseOptions: Between tracks, the Baroness opens her estate armory — light/medium 'Mechs and vehicles from House Adaire's guard, 2D6 of 8+ (she parts with her iron reluctantly). No assaults.

tracks.name: The Orji Laager
tracks.situation:
The blockade lives on the supply laager out on the Orji flats — fuel bladders, ammunition pallets, and a comm mast that ties the three road strongpoints together, all ringed by a light guard. Cut its throat and the strongpoints go blind and hungry inside a day. The Baroness wants it done fast, before the raiders grasp that the capital has teeth.

A strike is about the target, not the ground. Get to the laager, pick the comm mast out among the dumps, and put it and the fuel down; the guard matters only as far as it stands between you and the objective. Wreck the heart of the blockade and the strongpoints come apart without your ever fighting them.
tracks.deployment: Long edges. The Combine (Defender) sets up before Initiative in its own half, its guard around four objective structures near center — three Medium supply dumps and one comm mast (Level 2 building, 30 damage / AS 6). One dump is secretly recorded as the fuel bladder. You (Attacker) enter half your force on your home edge Turn 1, the rest from a short edge Turn 2.

objectives.text: Case the Laager — scan 2 structures, or find the comm mast.
Screen the Dumps — keep half your force within reach of the structures through Turn 4.
Cut the Cord — destroy the comm mast.
Fire the Dumps — identify and destroy the fuel bladder.
Hold the Heart — comm mast still standing at track end.

tracks.specialRules: Scanning follows Strike reveal rules (a scanned structure's role becomes known; the fuel bladder can be identified). When the fuel bladder is destroyed, every unit within 2 hexes takes 10 damage (AS 2). A destroyed road hex adds to Roads Wrecked.
tracks.trackEnd: Default.
tracks.salvagePolicy: Exchange (wrecks fall on Adaire land; you take 1/4 value in SP).

forks.trigger: You gutted the laager; the raiders mass to retake it before the strongpoints starve.
forks.consequence: Hold the wrecked laager long enough to finish it and the blockade breaks.

forks.trigger: The strike stalled and the cordon is closing with your force deep in raider ground.
forks.consequence: Fight your strike force back out through a hardening blockade line.

tracks.name: They Come for the Laager
tracks.situation:
The laager's heart is broken but not yet ash, and the raiders know that if they retake the Orji flats before the fires finish, the blockade holds. They come off the road strongpoints in strength to throw you off the wreckage you just took.

You hold the gutted laager while your demolition finishes the job — a perimeter on open ground against a force that has to move fast or lose everything. Hold to the clock and the strongpoints, cut off and starving, fold on their own; break, and the raiders re-knit the cordon around Gardena with your bonus inside it.
tracks.deployment: Short edges. You (Defender) hold one-third of your force off-map (arriving end of Turn 1, own half); the rest sets up within 6 hexes of your home edge (12" AS; 12/18" at Scale 2+), the demolition markers at center. The Combine (Attacker) enters Turn 1.

objectives.text: Hold the Laager — half your force within 4 hexes of center at end of Turn 3 (6/12" Turn 4 at Scale 2+).
Finish the Job — no demolition marker retaken (enemy-controlled) through end of Turn 6.
Retake the Flats — control 2 demolition markers at end of Turn 6.
Overpower — more non-crippled BV/PV near center at track end.

tracks.specialRules: Holding the laager through Turn 6 breaks the blockade (contract victory). A destroyed road hex adds to Roads Wrecked.
tracks.trackEnd: End of Turn 6 (Turn 8 AS at Scale 2+).
tracks.salvagePolicy: Exchange (estate land).

forks.trigger: The laager stands with you on it, or the raiders have it back.
forks.consequence: Contract closes — tally Roads Wrecked and settle the Baroness's purse and favor.

tracks.name: Out Through the Cordon
tracks.situation:
The strike did not land clean, and now the cordon is drawing tight with your force on the wrong side of it. The raiders have blocked the road back to Gardena; the Baroness's iron — and your contract — depend on getting it home.

A breakthrough is a race, not a brawl. Punch a hole in the cordon and get the bulk of your force across it before the raiders seal the gap. Crippled machines that make it out still make it out; what you leave behind, the blockade keeps.
tracks.deployment: Long edges. The Combine (Defender) sets up within 6 hexes of the Gardena-side edge (12" AS), blocking the road; you (Attacker) enter from the opposite edge on Turn 1.

objectives.text: Cross the Cordon — get half your force by BV/PV across the center line.
Seal the Road — keep half your force engaging the breakout for 2 consecutive turns.
Break Out — exit half your force (by count) off the Gardena-side edge; crippled units that exit still count.
Bag Them — cripple or destroy half the breakout force before it exits.
Bloody Nose — first side to destroy 25% of the enemy scores it; simultaneous = both score.

tracks.specialRules: Units exiting the Gardena-side edge return to the Baroness's service (recovered). A destroyed road hex adds to Roads Wrecked.
tracks.trackEnd: Default (one side has no 'Mechs in play, or Turn 10 / Turn 8 AS).
tracks.salvagePolicy: Exchange (estate land); the Defender recovers its own only if you fail to break out.

forks.trigger: Your force is out, or it is caught.
forks.consequence: Contract closes — tally Roads Wrecked and settle what the Baroness owes.

Vitreum can rebuild a factory; it cannot rebuild forty years of tooling. Get into the halls and pull the line out of their hands before they crate it or burn it — the recovery is the pay, not the battle.

b.employer: Draconis Combine — DCMS raiding command (Tai-i Marika Oda's raid on the works)

b.blurb: Strip the Fox Armory for the Dragon — crate Vitreum's jigs and prototypes and lift them off Pascagoula before a merc recovery force can pry them loose.

The Vitreum line — tooling, templates, both prototypes — must be crated and lifted before a recovery force can be scraped together, and technicians cannot work under fire. Hold the works and the loading yards, and put the March's vehicle plant on the Dragon's books.

hotspots.situation:
Pascagoula is a hard little world — one baked desert continent, barely any water, fewer than a million people, and nothing the wider Reach would notice but for a single asset. In Garnet City, the assembly halls of Vitreum Rolling Works stamp out Fox Armored Cars and Pegasus scout hover tanks for militias across the Draconis March. It is a poor world (D-D-C-D-C) with one rich vein, and everyone who fights along this border rides Vitreum's iron whether they know the name or not.

A week ago a Combine raiding force came down out of the dark and took Garnet City in a night. They did not come to hold a desert nobody wants — they came for the line. Right now DCMS armor sits in the loading yards while Combine technicians strip the assembly halls: the jigs, the master templates, the two prototype hulls the company had not yet fielded. Vitreum can raise another factory in a year. It cannot rebuild forty years of tooling, and it cannot let a Combine plant start turning out Foxes and Pegasi with a Suns-district serial number.

So the company hires you, because a world this small never sees an AFFS regiment in time. Vitreum pays in cash, not glory, and it is precise about the terms: it wants the tooling and the prototypes back, not a battle that levels what's left of the halls. The wrecks belong to the company; the recovery is the prize. Get into the works, pull the line loose from the Combine's hands, and get it out before the raiders can crate it or burn it. Every jig you save rides home; every one you leave, the Combine keeps or torches.

contract.constraints: Salvage Exchange (the company keeps the wrecks; you take the cash equivalent) — the recovery, not the battlefield salvage, is what pays here. Command House (a Vitreum security liaison rides with you).
contract.additionalRequirements: Track Scale 2; minimum fielded force 4,500 BV / 180 PV. A fast element helps — the raiders will run if pried loose.
contract.bonus: Recover the line — bring the tooling and both prototypes out intact and Vitreum Rolling Works pays a production bonus (500 SP) and +1 Reputation with the March's corporate contractors. Let the line burn and the bonus is forfeit.

SUCCESS pries the line loose and the raiders run (t2a, Pursuit across the flats). FAILURE bogs the raid and the works must be abandoned (t2b, Retreat covering the plant crews). The tree ends after Track 2.

Company minders. The Vitreum liaison flags every hall you damage — each assembly-hall building you destroy is -1 to the recovery bonus roll.
The line fights. Two plant-defense vehicles (Fox Armored Cars, green crews) join you — the works' own iron, driven by volunteers.
Blistering heat. Pascagoula runs 42 C at the equator — any 'Mech that runs or jumps gains +1 heat that turn (AS: -1 to-hit if it used its full move).
Sandstorm. Spotting beyond 6 hexes fails on a 1-2 (1D6) for the first 3 turns.
Roll twice, ignore repeats.

missionBrief.tally: Halls Burned — each assembly-hall building destroyed (by anyone) across the contract counts 1. At 3+, the line is crippled: -1 to the recovery bonus and no +1 Reputation.

namedCharacters.name: Tai-i Marika Oda
namedCharacters.rule: Leads the raid and runs a fast delaying action if pried loose. If killed, the Combine force is -2 Initiative for the rest of that track (Commander rule).

missionBrief.purchaseOptions: Between tracks, a Vitreum field list — light/medium 'Mechs and combat vehicles (heavy on the company's own hover and wheeled iron), 2D6 of 7+. No assaults.

tracks.name: The Garnet City Works
tracks.situation:
Garnet City is a company town wrapped around one asset — the assembly halls where Vitreum stamps out Foxes and Pegasi for half the district's militias. The Combine holds it now: DCMS armor in the loading yards, Combine technicians inside stripping the line for shipment. The jigs, the master templates, the two prototype hulls the company never fielded — all of it is being crated while you watch.

An objective raid is a smash-and-grab against the clock. Get into the works, secure the marked tooling and the prototypes before the Combine can ship them or torch them, and get out; the armor in the yards matters only as far as it stands between you and the line. Every jig you tag rides home with the company; every one you leave, the Combine keeps or burns to slag.
tracks.deployment: Long edges, industrial map. The Combine (Defender) sets up within 6 hexes of center, its armor screening four objective structures — three tooling jigs (Medium buildings) and one prototype bay near center. One jig is secretly recorded as the master-template vault. You (Attacker) enter Turn 1.

objectives.text: Breach the Works — get a unit adjacent to any marked structure.
Screen the Line — keep half your force within reach of the structures through Turn 4.
Secure the Tooling — control (adjacent, no enemy adjacent) 2 of the 3 jigs at end of Turn 5.
Save the Vault — identify and secure the master-template vault.
Scorch the Line — destroy 2 of the marked structures.

tracks.specialRules: Scanning follows Objective Raid reveal rules (a scanned structure's role becomes known; the master-template vault can be identified). A jig or the prototype bay secured intact is recovered (rides out with you). A structure destroyed by either side adds to Halls Burned.
tracks.trackEnd: End of Turn 8, or all marked structures resolved.
tracks.salvagePolicy: Exchange (the company keeps the wrecks; you take 1/4 value in SP). Recovered tooling is the contract's prize, not battlefield salvage.

forks.trigger: You pried the line loose; the raiders are pulling back across the Vitreum flats to their DropShip.
forks.consequence: Run them down before they regroup — and before they can call the ship down for a hot extraction.

forks.trigger: The raid bogged in the yards; the Combine is bringing up weight and the works cannot be held.
forks.consequence: Cover the plant crews and the tooling you did grab as they pull out of Garnet City.

tracks.name: Run Them Off Vitreum
tracks.situation:
The line is loose and the raiders know it — they are falling back across the Vitreum flats toward their DropShip's landing ground, hauling what tooling they still hold. Catch them in the open desert and you take back the rest; let them make the ship and it lifts with forty years of Vitreum's craft in its hold.

A pursuit is about pinning, not chasing. Force the raiders to turn and fight and their laden transports stop; get past the rear guard and the transports are yours. Let that guard fight a clean delaying action across the dunes and the Combine lifts with the prize — and the March militias that ride Vitreum's iron feel the loss for years.
tracks.deployment: Long edges, open desert. The Combine (Defender/quarry) enters its home edge Turn 1 and must move toward the far, DropShip edge; its transports are laden and move at half speed. You (Attacker/pursuer) enter the same home edge Turn 2 at full speed. No Battlefield Support this track.

objectives.text: Run Them Down — engage or scan half the Combine column by end of Turn 4.
Keep Moving — keep half your transports advancing toward the DropShip edge for 3 consecutive turns.
No Quarter — destroy or cripple half the column before it exits.
Make the Ship — exit half the column (by count) off the DropShip edge.
First Blood — first side to destroy 25% of the enemy scores it; simultaneous = both score.

tracks.specialRules: Combine transports are the column's slow half (move at half speed). Each transport that exits the DropShip edge carries recovered tooling out of your reach (toward the Combine's contract win).
tracks.trackEnd: Turn 10 (Turn 8 AS), or the column has no transports left on-map.
tracks.salvagePolicy: Pool-draft on the pursuit's kills; a recovered transport returns its tooling to the company (Exchange cash to you).

forks.trigger: The raiders are run down, or they made the ship.
forks.consequence: Contract closes — tally Halls Burned and settle Vitreum's production bonus.

tracks.name: Get the Line Out
tracks.situation:
The raid bogged in the loading yards and the Combine is bringing up its heavy armor; Garnet City cannot be held. The job now is smaller and harder — get the plant crews and the tooling you did pry loose out of the city and onto the road west before the Combine closes the last gate. The works are lost; the people and the craft do not have to be.

A retreat is a fighting withdrawal, not a rout. You cover the evacuation column while it clears the map, trading the yards you cannot keep for the time the crews need. Get them out and Vitreum rebuilds around what you saved; let the Combine catch the column and the company loses its future along with its factory.
tracks.deployment: Short edges, same-edge start. You (Defender) enter from the Combine's edge Turn 1, escorting the evacuation markers (plant crews and tooling transports) toward your home edge; the Combine (Attacker) enters its own edge Turn 2.

objectives.text: Run Them Down — scan or engage half your units in the Defender's half by end of Turn 4.
Break Contact — exit at least one evacuation marker off your home edge.
Get Them Out — exit half the evacuation markers off your home edge; a marker that exits counts even if escorted crippled.
Cut the Column — destroy 2 evacuation markers.
Hammer — first side to destroy 25% of the enemy scores it; simultaneous = both score.

tracks.specialRules: Evacuation markers move at half a Medium 'Mech's walk. A marker destroyed adds to Halls Burned (the craft aboard is lost). Each marker exited safely is tooling or crew recovered for the company.
tracks.trackEnd: Turn 10.
tracks.salvagePolicy: Exchange; the Combine recovers its own only if it wins.

forks.trigger: The column is out, or it is caught in the yards.
forks.consequence: Contract closes — tally Halls Burned and settle what Vitreum owes.

hotspots.title: Atlantis Under

a.employer: Federated Suns — AFFS coastal garrison (evacuation contract)

a.situation: Protection is falling; what is not yet decided is who its people belong to when it does. Evacuation columns are streaming into Atlantis City's harbor while there is still a harbor to reach — cover them to the docks and onto the boats. You are paid on lives out, not ground held; every soul afloat is leverage denied.

b.employer: Draconis Combine — DCMS landing command (Chu-sa Hideo Yamada's assault)

contract.constraints: Command House (a DCMS liaison drives the landing). The Combine wants the harbor whole and the population as leverage — catch the columns before they reach the water, don't sink the boats.
contract.additionalRequirements: Track Scale 2; minimum fielded force 4,000 BV / 160 PV. Amphibious or jump-capable designs strongly favored — this is a water world.
contract.bonus: Take the harbor — cut off half Atlantis City's evacuation and hold the docks and the Combine grants +1 Reputation and a landing bonus.

b.blurb: Drive the Atlantis landing for the Dragon — race the boats to the harbor and cut off the columns before they reach the water; a population is leverage.
b.situation: Chu-sa Yamada's landing is ashore, and the prize is not the ground — it is the harbor whole and the people still on it. A population in hand ends this campaign on the Dragon's terms. Race the evacuation to the water, cut the columns off before they reach the docks, and sink nothing we will want later.

hotspots.situation:
Protection is a blue world — nine parts water to one part land — and its half-billion people live on scattered islands and the single continent the maps call Atlantis City. It is a prosperous place, all aquaculture and shipping (it rates A for agriculture), the kind of quiet border world that has never needed to think hard about war. In the spring of 3151 that ends: a Draconis Combine landing force comes down out of a low orbit onto the Atlantis continent, and the Federated Suns garrison holding Protection is far too thin to throw it back.

What the garrison can still do is get the people out. Atlantis City's harbor is loading every hull that floats, and evacuation columns are streaming down to the docks while there is still a dock to reach. The AFFS commander cannot spare the regulars to both fight the landing and shepherd the civilians, so she hires your command for the second job and the harder one. The contract is blunt about it: you are paid on people saved, not ground held. The Suns are going to lose Protection. They are not going to lose Protection's people.

The nuance is a House contract run at a civilian's pace. Command is AFFS House — a liaison rides with the evacuation and can commit you to cover a column. The Combine claims the wrecks, so salvage is Exchange and you take the cash. And the Combine wants the harbor intact and the population as leverage, which means every column that reaches the boats is not just lives saved but a bargaining chip denied. Get them aboard and gone; whatever the Combine cuts off from the water, it keeps.

contract.additionalRequirements: Track Scale 2; minimum fielded force 4,000 BV / 160 PV. Amphibious or jump-capable designs strongly favored — this is a water world.
contract.bonus: Full evacuation — get the civilian columns out across both tracks and the AFFS grants +1 Reputation and battle-loss compensation (75% SP replacement) on any 'Mech lost covering the docks.

missionBrief.behindScenes: A water-world evacuation. Track 1 is the fighting withdrawal to the Atlantis docks; the Track 1 result drives the branch. SUCCESS gets the columns to the water and the boats load (t2a, Defend the pier). FAILURE cuts the survivors off from the harbor (t2b, Breakthrough across the causeway to the next island). The tree ends after Track 2.

complications.effect: None.
Rising tide. At the start of Turn 4 the seaward hex rows rise a level (Level 1 water becomes Level 2); any unit caught there makes a Piloting check.
Refugee crush. A civilian column jams a road hex you need — moving through it costs double, and any fire through that hex is a -1 Reputation flag.
Naval gunfire. One friendly Battlefield Support artillery strike is free this track (an AFFS destroyer standing offshore).
Liaison commits. The AFFS liaison pushes one of your units to hold a forward pier 3 hexes ahead of your line.
Roll twice, ignore repeats.

namedCharacters.name: Chu-sa Hideo Yamada

missionBrief.purchaseOptions: Between tracks, an AFFS coastal-defense list — light/medium 'Mechs, hover and amphibious vehicles, 2D6 of 8+. No assaults (nothing that bogs on a water world).

tracks.name: The Atlantis Docks
tracks.situation:
The Combine came down onto the Atlantis continent and the garrison could not hold the beaches, so now the harbor is the whole battle. The evacuation columns are streaming down to the docks, and the boats are filling as fast as the ramps allow — but the Combine is right behind the columns, and it wants the harbor whole and the people in it.

A retreat is a fighting withdrawal, not a rout. You cover the civilian columns as they fall back to the water, trading the streets you cannot hold for the minutes the boats need to load. Every column that reaches the docks is a town that lives; every one the Combine cuts off from the water is a bargaining chip in Combine hands.
tracks.deployment: Short edges, same-edge start, coastal map (the seaward third is Level 1 water; the docks line your home edge). You (Defender) enter from the Combine's edge Turn 1, escorting the civilian markers toward the docks on your home edge; the Combine (Attacker) enters its own edge Turn 2.

Reach the Docks — exit at least one civilian marker off your home (dock) edge.
Load the Boats — exit half the civilian markers off the dock edge; a marker that reaches the docks counts even if escorted crippled.
Cut Them Off — destroy 2 civilian markers before they reach the water.
Hammer — first side to destroy 25% of the enemy scores it; simultaneous = both score.

tracks.trackEnd: Turn 10.

forks.trigger: The columns made the docks; the fleet is loading the last of them.
forks.consequence: Hold the loading pier until the final hull casts off.

forks.trigger: The docks fell before the columns cleared; the survivors are cut off from the water.
forks.consequence: Break the surviving column through the Combine's causeway block to the fishing harbor on the next island.

tracks.name: The Last Hull Out
tracks.situation:
The columns made it, and the harbor is a chaos of ramps and casting lines as the last transports swallow the last of Atlantis City's people. The Combine is throwing everything it has at the pier now — take the harbor before the fleet sails and the ships become hostages, the evacuation a surrender. So you hold the pier.

This is the simplest kind of fight and the hardest: stand on the loading pier and do not move until the horn sounds. A defense is a clock, and the clock is the boarding ramps. Hold to the end and the fleet sails with Protection's people aboard; break, and the Combine takes the harbor, the hulls, and everyone still on them.
tracks.deployment: Short edges, harbor map. You (Defender) hold one-third of your force off-map (arriving end of Turn 1, own half); the rest sets up within 6 hexes of your home (pier) edge (12" AS; 12/18" at Scale 2+), the loading ramps (immobile markers) at your edge. The Combine (Attacker) enters Turn 1. Battlefield Support allowed (the offshore destroyer).

Cast Off — no loading ramp reached (enemy-adjacent) through end of Turn 6.
Storm the Harbor — reach (adjacent) 2 loading ramps.
Overpower — more non-crippled BV/PV near the pier at track end.

tracks.trackEnd: End of Turn 6 (Turn 8 AS at Scale 2+).
tracks.salvagePolicy: Exchange (the AFFS claims Combine wrecks).

forks.trigger: The fleet sails, or the harbor falls.
forks.consequence: Contract closes — tally Souls Lost and settle the AFFS's favor.

tracks.name: The Causeway
tracks.situation:
The docks fell too fast, and the last columns are trapped on the wrong side of the water with the Combine between them and any boat. There is one way out — the old stone causeway that runs to the fishing harbor on the next island — and a Combine blocking force sitting square across it. The people cannot swim to safety; you have to open the road.

A breakthrough is a race, not a brawl. Punch a hole in the causeway block and push the surviving column across before the Combine can seal it. The causeway is a kilometer of open stone with water on both sides — no cover, no clever flank, just the road and the will to force it. Get them across to the harbor and they sail from there; fail, and the column ends on the causeway.
tracks.deployment: Long edges, causeway map (the center is a raised stone causeway flanked by Level 1 water). The Combine (Defender) sets up within 6 hexes of the harbor-side edge (12" AS), blocking the causeway; you (Attacker) enter from the mainland edge Turn 1, escorting the civilian markers.

Hold the Block — keep half your force engaging the breakout for 2 consecutive turns.
Get Them Across — exit half the civilian markers off the harbor-side edge; crippled escorts that exit still count.
Close the Road — destroy 2 civilian markers on the causeway.
Bloody Nose — first side to destroy 25% of the enemy scores it; simultaneous = both score.

tracks.trackEnd: Default (one side has no 'Mechs in play, or Turn 10 / Turn 8 AS).
tracks.salvagePolicy: Exchange; the Defender recovers its own only if you fail to break through.

forks.consequence: Contract closes — tally Souls Lost and settle what the AFFS owes.

hotspots.title: Old Ghosts
hotspots.employer: Federated Suns — AFFS Draconis March command

Lead the assault that throws them back before the foothold hardens into a siege. Spend what you must, but the memorial city and its dead are not yours to shell.

b.employer: Draconis Combine — DCMS landing command (Tai-sa Katsuo Nomura's foothold)

contract.constraints: Command House (a DCMS liaison rides with the landing). The foothold is meant to break the March's nerve on the one world it cannot stomach losing — hold it and drive on the memorial city.
contract.additionalRequirements: Track Scale 2; minimum fielded force 5,000 BV / 200 PV.
contract.bonus: Break the March — hold the Kentares foothold and take the memorial city and the Combine grants +1 Reputation and a propaganda bonus for the one flag that would cut deepest.

b.blurb: Hold the Kentares foothold for the Dragon — break something in the March that armor can't mend by taking the one world it will never forgive losing.
b.situation: Tai-sa Nomura's landing holds ground on the one world the March cannot think straight about, and that is the point. Every hour the Dragon's flag stands on Kentares, something in the Suns' border breaks a little further. Hold the coastal plain against the counterblow — the ghost of 2796 holds no power over soldiers who refuse it.

hotspots.situation:
Every soldier on the Draconis March border knows the name Kentares. Three and a half centuries ago the Combine answered a dead Coordinator's grief with an order that emptied a whole world — the Kentares Massacre, millions of civilians killed, a wound the Federated Suns has never let scar over. The world recovered its people slowly and never recovered the memory; the great remembrance park outside the capital keeps the names, and the March keeps the grudge. Kentares is a modest world of warm seas and insect life, but its name carries a weight no industrial rating can measure.

In the ilClan war, a Combine landing force has set down on Kentares again and dug a foothold into the coastal plain. It has not come for the world's thin industry. It has come because taking Kentares, of all worlds, would break something in the March that armor cannot mend — and because some Combine officers would like to prove the old ghost has no power over them. The AFFS reads it exactly that way, and it will not have it.

Before the foothold hardens into a siege, the Draconis March command hires your command to lead the assault that throws it back. The terms are a House contract run at a grudge's pace: the Suns claim the Combine wrecks, they compensate your losses, and they make very clear that Kentares is the one world where the March will spend anything. Every hour the Combine holds is an hour the ghost of 2796 walks the newsfeeds. Hit them now, hit them hard, and Kentares stays Davion.

contract.additionalRequirements: Track Scale 2; minimum fielded force 5,000 BV / 200 PV.
contract.bonus: Throw them off — clear Kentares across both tracks and the March grants +1 Reputation and battle-loss compensation (75% SP replacement) on any 'Mech lost taking the foothold. Wreck the memorial in the saving of it and the bonus is withheld.

SUCCESS routs the landing (t2a, Pursuit to the DropShips). FAILURE lets the Combine drive for the memorial city (t2b, Defend the memorial line). The tree ends after Track 2.

The memory. A civilian remembrance procession crosses the field; any friendly unit that fires through its hex takes a -1 Reputation flag (Kentares does not forgive).
Militia rally. Kentares' planetary militia sends a lance (two medium 'Mechs, or a vehicle element; green, Gunnery 5 / Piloting 6) to fight beside you — they will not retreat.
Ash haze. Industrial murk over the plain — spotting beyond 8 hexes fails on a 1-2 (1D6) for the first 3 turns.

namedCharacters.name: Tai-sa Katsuo Nomura
namedCharacters.rule: Leads the foothold from the front and knows exactly what world he stands on. If killed, the Combine force is -2 Initiative for the rest of that track (Commander rule).

missionBrief.purchaseOptions: Between tracks, an AFFS Draconis March list — light/medium 'Mechs and combat vehicles, 2D6 of 8+. No assaults.

tracks.name: The Blood-Ground
tracks.situation:
The Combine foothold sits on the coastal plain between the landing beaches and the memorial city, dug in overnight and waiting for you. There is no clever line of approach — the ground is open and the Combine has ranged it — but there is a clock, and the clock is on your side only as long as you keep moving. Wait, and the foothold becomes a fortress; the Suns hired a hammer, not a siege engine.

An assault is a hammer. You come at the Combine line hard and fast, break it before it can consolidate, and take the ground while the taking is still cheap. The Combine commander means to stand and bleed you on the open plain until the daylight and your momentum both run out. Break his line first, take the center of the foothold, and Kentares stays Davion.
tracks.deployment: Long edges. The Combine (Defender) sets up within 5 hexes of its home edge (10" AS) before Initiative; no minefield or immobile Battlefield Support. You (Attacker) enter Turn 1.

objectives.text: Press the Attack — engage the Combine for 2 consecutive turns.
Stand Fast — the Combine keeps its whole force on-map for 3 turns.
Break the Foothold — reduce the Combine to half its starting BV/PV (tie = neither).
Take the Ground — more non-crippled BV/PV within 4 hexes of the foothold center at track end.
Cut the Head — destroy the enemy commander's unit.

tracks.trackEnd: Default.
tracks.salvagePolicy: Winner-all (SP at your salvage %; Exchange here = 1/4 value in cash).

forks.trigger: The foothold broke; the Combine is falling back to its landing ground.
forks.consequence: Run them down before they lift — and before they can call it a raid instead of a rout.

forks.trigger: The assault stalled and the Combine is driving for the memorial city itself.
forks.consequence: Hold the line at the Kentares memorial — the one place the March will not lose again.

tracks.name: Run for the DropShips
tracks.situation:
The foothold is broken and the Combine is streaming back toward its landing ground on the coastal flats. This is where a rout becomes a rout: catch the retreating column in the open and Kentares is not just held but avenged, the Combine bloodied on the one world it should never have touched again.

A pursuit is about pinning, not chasing. Force the rear guard to turn and the column stalls under your guns; slip past it and the slow transports are yours. Let them fight a clean withdrawal and the Combine lifts to spin this as a probe — and the March loses the chance to make Kentares mean something other than grief.
tracks.deployment: Long edges. The Combine (Defender/quarry) enters its home edge Turn 1 and must move toward the far, landing-ground edge; its transports move at half speed. You (Attacker/pursuer) enter the same home edge Turn 2 at full speed. No Battlefield Support this track.

objectives.text: Run Them Down — engage or scan half the Combine column by end of Turn 4.
Keep Moving — keep half the column advancing toward the landing edge for 3 consecutive turns.
No Quarter — destroy or cripple half the column before it exits.
Make the Ships — exit half the column (by count) off the landing edge.
First Blood — first side to destroy 25% of the enemy scores it; simultaneous = both score.

tracks.specialRules: Combine transports are the column's slow half (move at half speed).
tracks.trackEnd: Turn 10 (Turn 8 AS), or the column has no units left on-map.
tracks.salvagePolicy: Pool-draft (wrecks pooled, alternate picks, winner first); Exchange cash to you.

forks.trigger: The column is run down, or it made the ships.
forks.consequence: Contract closes — tally Old Ghosts and settle the March's grudging favor.

tracks.name: The Memorial Line
tracks.situation:
The assault did not land, and now the Combine is driving for the memorial city — the walled remembrance park where Kentares keeps the names of its dead millions. Of every objective on this world, this is the one the Federated Suns will spend anything to hold. If the Combine plants its banner over the Kentares memorial, no communique in the March can undo it.

So you hold the line at the memorial gates. A defense is a clock, and the clock is the March relief racing in from Robinson. Trade the outer districts for time, keep the Combine off the remembrance park, and the relief arrives to a world that stood. Break, and the ghost of 2796 gets a new and terrible sequel.
tracks.deployment: Short edges. You (Defender) hold one-third of your force off-map (arriving end of Turn 1, own half); the rest sets up within 6 hexes of your home edge (12" AS; 12/18" at Scale 2+), the memorial structures (Medium buildings, objective markers) at center. The Combine (Attacker) enters Turn 1.

objectives.text: Hold the Gates — half your force within 4 hexes of the memorial at end of Turn 3 (6/12" Turn 4 at Scale 2+).
Keep the Names — no memorial structure destroyed or enemy-held through end of Turn 6.
Plant the Banner — control (adjacent, no defender adjacent) the central memorial at end of Turn 6.
Overpower — more non-crippled BV/PV near the memorial at track end.

tracks.specialRules: Holding the memorial through Turn 6 stands the line (contract victory). Each memorial structure destroyed adds to Old Ghosts.
tracks.trackEnd: End of Turn 6 (Turn 8 AS at Scale 2+).
tracks.salvagePolicy: Winner-all (SP at your salvage %); Exchange cash to you.

forks.consequence: Contract closes — tally Old Ghosts and settle what the March owes.

hotspots.title: Conqueror's Pride
hotspots.employer: Draconis Combine — Proserpina Prefecture warlord (DCMS liaison)

a.blurb: Hold a Kurita capital for the Dragon — keep the Davion raid out of Conqueror's Pride until the relief burns in from Benjamin, and take their machines as prizes.
a.situation: A Davion raiding force is down on Proserpina to burn what the line regiments left behind, and the warlord has iron enough for the palace and not a company more. Hold the approaches to Conqueror's Pride until relief burns in from Benjamin. The liaison wants Davion machines taken as prizes — and a capital saved in ashes is no victory.

b.employer: Federated Suns — AFFS deep-raiding command (Leftenant Colonel Cass Hollis's raid)

contract.constraints: Command Independent — a deep cross-border raid runs on its own initiative, no liaison to answer to. Salvage decent — take what Kurita hardware you can drag home.

b.blurb: Raid deep for the Suns — jump the border and burn what the Combine left lightly held; take Conqueror's Pride's district and be gone before the relief arrives.
b.situation: While the Dragon's regiments drive into the March, Leftenant Colonel Hollis is repaying the visit. Proserpina is a proud prefecture capital held by a palace guard and its own certainty that war happens to lesser worlds. Take the government district of Conqueror's Pride, burn what was left lightly held, and lift before the relief lands.

hotspots.situation:
For once, you fight for the Dragon. Proserpina is the capital of its prefecture — five continents of tainted air and reptile-haunted marsh under a dim orange sun, and a proud old Combine world that has not seen a hostile 'Mech in a lifetime. Its city, Conqueror's Pride, is a Kurita capital in the fullest sense: shrines, government halls, and a citizenry raised to believe the border wars happen to other, lesser worlds.

The ilClan war has arrived to prove them wrong. With the Combine's line regiments driving forward into the Federated Suns' Draconis March, a Davion raiding force has jumped the border the other way and come down on Proserpina to burn what the Combine left lightly held. The prefecture warlord has iron enough to hold the palace and not a company more, so he does the thing his pride can barely stomach: he hires outland mercenaries to hold his capital's gates.

The nuance is a Combine contract, and it comes with Combine expectations. Command is House — a DCMS liaison rides at your shoulder and expects the Davion machines taken as prizes, not scrap. The Combine pays well and shares its salvage, because it wants Davion hardware to study. And it wants Conqueror's Pride held whole: a capital saved in ashes is a poor kind of victory, and the warlord will remember which mercenaries understood that. Hold the gates until the relief burns in from Benjamin, and you are the hired guns who saved a Kurita capital. Break, and you are the ones who let it fall.

contract.bonus: Save the capital — hold Conqueror's Pride across both tracks and the warlord grants +1 Reputation with the Draconis Combine and a captured-'Mech prize (one Davion chassis crippled and claimed on the field, repaired to your roster) at contract end. SUCCESS recoils the raid (t2a, Pursuit to the landing zone). FAILURE lets the Davions into the city (t2b, Pushback through the government district). The tree ends after Track 2.

DCMS honor. The liaison demands a prize: if you destroy the Davion commander's unit rather than crippling and claiming it, take a -1 Reputation flag with the Combine.
Prefecture levy. A Combine militia lance (two mediums, or a vehicle element; regular, Gunnery 4 / Piloting 5) of Conqueror's Pride locals joins you.

namedCharacters.rule: Leads the Davion raid; a bold officer who hits fast and knows when to run. If killed, the Federated Suns force is -2 Initiative for the rest of that track (Commander rule).

tracks.name: The Approaches to Conqueror's Pride
tracks.situation:
The Davion column comes off the Amerigo plain toward the capital along the only two ways in — a highway and a rail cut that meet at a junction three kilometers short of the government district. Hold that junction and the raid stalls in the open, where the warlord's few real guns can reach it; lose it, and the Davions are into the streets of a Kurita capital.

A defense is a clock, and your clock is the Combine relief burning in from Benjamin. You hold the junction and the approaches, trading the outer ground for the hours the warlord needs. The DCMS liaison at your shoulder expects the line to hold and the Davion machines taken whole. Hold, and Conqueror's Pride never hears a shot in its streets.
tracks.deployment: Short edges. You (Defender) hold one-third of your force off-map (arriving end of Turn 1, own half); the rest sets up within 6 hexes of your home edge (12" AS; 12/18" at Scale 2+), the highway/rail junction (objective) at center. The Federated Suns (Attacker) enters Turn 1. Tainted-atmosphere rules apply (see complications).

objectives.text: Hold the Junction — half your force within 4 hexes of the junction at end of Turn 3 (6/12" Turn 4 at Scale 2+).
Bar the Road — no Davion unit reaches your home (capital) edge through end of Turn 6.
Force the Approach — get 3 units adjacent to the capital edge by end of Turn 6.
Overpower — more non-crippled BV/PV near the junction at track end.

tracks.trackEnd: End of Turn 6 (Turn 8 AS at Scale 2+).

forks.trigger: The approaches held; the Davion raid is pulling back to its landing zone.
forks.consequence: Run the raiders down before they lift with their pride intact.

forks.trigger: The line bent and Davion 'Mechs are into the government district.
forks.consequence: Push them back out of Conqueror's Pride, block by block, before they fire the palace.

tracks.name: Break the Raid
tracks.situation:
The approaches held, and the Davion raiders are falling back across the Amerigo plain toward the landing zone where their DropShips wait. A raid that lifts clean is a raid the enemy repeats; a raid run down on the ground is a lesson, and the warlord wants it taught where his prefecture can watch.

A pursuit is about pinning, not chasing. Force the Davion rear guard to turn and the column stalls under your guns; slip past it and the slow transports are yours. Let them break contact cleanly and the raiders make the ships with their machines and their nerve intact — and the DCMS liaison counts every Davion hull you leave standing as a mark against you.

Keep Moving — keep half the column advancing toward the landing edge for 3 consecutive turns.
No Quarter — destroy or cripple half the column before it exits.
Make the Ships — exit half the column (by count) off the landing edge.
Claim a Prize — cripple (not destroy) the Davion commander's unit and hold the field near it at track end.

tracks.trackEnd: Turn 10 (Turn 8 AS), or the column has no units left on-map.

tracks.name: Streets of Conqueror's Pride
tracks.situation:
The line bent and the Davion raiders are into Conqueror's Pride itself, trading fire among the shrines and government halls of a Kurita capital. This is the nightmare the warlord hired you to prevent, and there is no time for a careful plan — every turn the Davions hold the district is a turn closer to the palace and the propaganda coup of a burning Combine capital.

A pushback is a grind measured in blocks. You drive the Davions back through the streets, retaking the district hex by hex while the buildings channel the fight into brutal short-ranged exchanges. Push them out past the district edge and Conqueror's Pride is saved with its pride intact; stall in the streets, and the capital burns around both of you — every shrine that falls a mark against the mercenaries who were supposed to save it.
tracks.deployment: Long edges, dense urban map. The Federated Suns (Defender) sets up holding the government district (within 6 hexes of center, among Medium and Heavy buildings). You (Attacker) enter from your home edge Turn 1 and push toward and through the district. Buildings block line of sight and channel movement.

objectives.text: Retake the Blocks — more of your non-crippled BV/PV within 3 hexes of the district center at end of Turn 4.
Dig In — keep half your force in the district for 3 consecutive turns.
Drive Them Out — push 75% of the Davion force back across the far district edge and out by Turn 10.
Hold the Halls — keep one marked government building Davion-held at track end.
Make Them Bleed — destroy or cripple half the enemy force.

Now a rival command is down on the Ventrale plain carrying its own signed copy of the same contract, and the liaison has gone silent except for one ruling: the command still standing at week's end was 'always' the one hired. Settle it on the field, and settle it clean.

hotspots.blurb: A rival mercenary command landed on Mirach claiming your AFFS garrison contract, and the liaison won't say who's real until one of you is off the field. Settle it in the open.
hotspots.situation:
Mirach is a quiet prize — a temperate Draconis March world of two continents under four bright moons, seventh out from a dim red sun and close enough to Robinson that the March keeps a standing garrison contract on it. That contract came up for renewal, and you won it. Or so your paymaster said.

Because a second mercenary command has just dropped onto the Ventrale plain outside Cingulum, flying its own colors and carrying its own signed copy of the same garrison contract. Somewhere between the March's regional command and two sets of lawyers, Mirach was sold twice. The AFFS liaison has gone conveniently silent; the only thing he will say is that the command still standing at the end of the week is the one that was 'always' hired. So this is the oldest mercenary story there is — two outfits, one contract, and a field to settle it on.

Merc against merc is its own kind of war. There is no House doctrine to hide behind and no liaison to blame, just your reputation against theirs, in front of a world that will remember which command kept its word and which one folded. Beat them cleanly and Mirach's garrison — and its pay — are yours; lose, and you are the outfit that got run off a world it was hired to hold.

contract.constraints: Command Independent (no House liaison commands you — you answer to the contract and your own reputation). Salvage decent (a contested field, wrecks split by the draft).

SUCCESS breaks the rival and you run them off (t2a, Pursuit). FAILURE loses you the field and you fall back on possession (t2b, Defend the garrison house). The tree ends after Track 2.

Contract lawyers. The liaison's paperwork is a mess — battle-loss compensation is void this contract (a jumped contract carries no clean guarantees).
A defector's tip. You see the rival's deployment before you set up (a poached tech sold you their drop plan).
Four-moon night. Mirach's moons wash out the dark (no night rules), but the Ventrale lowland hexes are tidal-soft ground — 1 extra MP to enter.
The Duke is watching. Collateral damage to the Cingulum outskirts is a -1 Reputation flag (Mirach's landholder wants a garrison, not a wrecking crew).
Roll twice, ignore repeats.

missionBrief.contractVictory: You: hold the field and keep the contract — win the meeting engagement in Track 1 and win Track 2. Rival command: take the field (win Track 1), or run you off the garrison (win Track 2b).
missionBrief.tally: Cingulum Collateral — each civilian structure on the city outskirts destroyed (by anyone) across the contract counts 1. At 3+, the Duke sours on both outfits: -1 Reputation and the retainer withheld.

namedCharacters.name: Colonel Dax Verrault
namedCharacters.rule: Leads the rival command and fights for the field, not glory — he pulls back the moment the contract's clearly lost. If killed, the rival is -2 Initiative for the rest of that track (Commander rule).

missionBrief.purchaseOptions: Between tracks, an open merc market — light/medium 'Mechs and combat vehicles from Mirach's spaceport traders, 2D6 of 7+. No assaults.

tracks.name: The Ventrale Plain
tracks.situation:
Both commands come down onto the open Ventrale plain outside Cingulum within an hour of each other, and there is no pretending it away — two mercenary outfits, one garrison contract, and a stretch of flat ground in sight of the city that the liaison will call 'the field.' Whoever holds it holds the claim.

A meeting engagement is decided by who seizes the center first and holds it. Get your weight onto the ground quickly and break the rival's line before it can consolidate, and the contract is yours to keep. Come in piecemeal, let them take the center, and you are the outfit explaining to the Duke why you lost a world you never fired a shot to defend.
tracks.deployment: Short edges. Both commands enter Turn 1 from opposite home edges; neither sets up in advance. The center third of the plain — the ground within sight of Cingulum — is the contested claim.

objectives.text: Seize the Ground — more of your non-crippled BV/PV in the center third than the rival at end of Turn 4.
Hold the Claim — the same at end of Turn 8.
Break Them — reduce the rival to half its starting BV/PV (tie = neither).
Colonel's Fall — destroy the rival commander's unit.

tracks.specialRules: Holding the center third at track end is 'the field' — the liaison rules the contract for whoever holds it. A destroyed Cingulum-outskirts structure adds to Cingulum Collateral.
tracks.trackEnd: Default (Turn 10 / Turn 8 AS, or one side has no 'Mechs in play).
tracks.salvagePolicy: Pool-draft (wrecks pooled, alternate picks, winner first).

forks.trigger: You broke the rival's line; they are pulling back to their DropShips.
forks.consequence: Run them off Mirach before they can spin it as a tactical withdrawal.

forks.trigger: The rival took the field; they are moving to occupy the garrison.
forks.consequence: Fall back on the garrison house in Cingulum and hold your claim until the liaison must rule.

tracks.name: Run Them Off Mirach
tracks.situation:
The rival broke on the Ventrale plain and now they are streaming back to their DropShips, hoping to lift and call it a 'reassessment' rather than a rout. A mercenary command that leaves under its own power keeps its name; one run down on the field does not. Chase them, and make sure the March — and the trade — knows exactly which outfit held Mirach.

A pursuit is about pinning, not chasing. Force the rear guard to turn and the column stalls; slip past it and their slow transports are yours. Let them break contact cleanly and they lift with their reputation intact — and yours a little cheaper for having let them.
tracks.deployment: Long edges. The rival command (Defender/quarry) enters its home edge Turn 1 and must move toward the far, landing-field edge; its transports move at half speed. You (Attacker/pursuer) enter the same home edge Turn 2 at full speed. No Battlefield Support this track.

objectives.text: Run Them Down — engage or scan half the rival column by end of Turn 4.
Keep Moving — keep half your transports advancing toward the landing edge for 3 consecutive turns.
No Quarter — destroy or cripple half the column before it exits.
Break Contact — exit half the column (by count) off the landing edge.
First Blood — first side to destroy 25% of the enemy scores it; simultaneous = both score.

tracks.specialRules: The rival's transports are the column's slow half (move at half speed).
tracks.trackEnd: Turn 10 (Turn 8 AS), or the column has no units left on-map.
tracks.salvagePolicy: Pool-draft (wrecks pooled, alternate picks, winner first).

forks.trigger: The rival is run down, or they made the ships.
forks.consequence: Contract closes — settle the Mirach garrison and your standing with the trade.

tracks.name: Hold the Garrison House
tracks.situation:
The field went to the rival, and now they are moving to occupy the Mirach garrison compound in Cingulum — because a liaison who won't choose between two contracts will, in the end, rule for whoever is physically sitting in the garrison house. So you fall back on the compound and dig in. Possession is nine-tenths of a jumped contract.

A defense is a clock, and the clock is the liaison's deadline to rule. Hold the compound past it and the contract defaults to the outfit still in the chairs; break, and you have handed Mirach to the command that beat you in the open. Trade the outer yards for time, keep them off the garrison house, and let the paperwork do the rest.
tracks.deployment: Short edges, compound map. You (Defender) hold one-third of your force off-map (arriving end of Turn 1, own half); the rest sets up within 6 hexes of your home edge (12" AS; 12/18" at Scale 2+), the garrison house (objective building) at center. The rival (Attacker) enters Turn 1.

objectives.text: Hold the Compound — half your force within 4 hexes of the garrison house at end of Turn 3 (6/12" Turn 4 at Scale 2+).
Keep the Keys — no enemy unit adjacent to the garrison house through end of Turn 6.
Take the House — control (adjacent, no defender adjacent) the garrison house at end of Turn 6.
Overpower — more non-crippled BV/PV near the garrison house at track end.

tracks.specialRules: Holding the garrison house through Turn 6 defaults the contract to you (contract victory). A destroyed Cingulum structure adds to Cingulum Collateral.
tracks.trackEnd: End of Turn 6 (Turn 8 AS at Scale 2+).
tracks.salvagePolicy: Pool-draft (wrecks pooled, alternate picks, winner first).

forks.consequence: Contract closes — tally Cingulum Collateral and settle which outfit keeps Mirach.

a.situation: A Capellan column is driving across the Saginaw plain for the Stannic Bridge — the one road into Fort Bourgogne, the span McCarron crossed twice. Neither side will destroy Star League lostech, so the bridge stands, and everything must come down that single hard road. Hold it; the March did not rebuild the fort for a third fall.

b.employer: Capellan Confederation — CCAF raiding command (Sang-shao Lian Cho, in the McCarron tradition)

contract.constraints: Command House (a CCAF liaison; Warrior House honor is observed — the Stannic Bridge is wanted whole to cross, not destroyed). Salvage Exchange (the Confederation claims the wrecks).
contract.additionalRequirements: Track Scale 2; minimum fielded force 5,000 BV / 200 PV.
contract.bonus: Crack the line — force the Stannic Bridge and take Fort Bourgogne where McCarron only managed twice: +1 Reputation with the Confederation and a warrior's honors.

b.blurb: Force the Stannic Bridge for the Chancellor — take Fort Bourgogne in the McCarron tradition and prove the Davion 'impregnable' fortress can fall a third time.
b.situation: Twice McCarron's Armored Cavalry crossed the Stannic Bridge and cracked the fortress the Davions call impregnable; Sang-shao Cho means to make it three. The bridge is wanted whole — it is the road in, not the target. Force the crossing in the open, break the line before Fort Bourgogne, and write the third proof yourself.

hotspots.blurb: A Capellan raiding force is driving on the Stannic Bridge and Fort Bourgogne — the fortress McCarron's Cavalry cracked twice. Hold the line the AFFS swears is impregnable.
hotspots.regionNote: Marlette is a Crucis March / Capellan-border world (not Draconis March proper) — a guest entry that showcases the Capellan Confederation as OpFor. Move to a Crucis-March pack later if desired.
hotspots.situation:
Marlette sits on the old Capellan frontier of the Federated Suns, a fortress world by habit and by history: three continents, two and a half billion people, and above it all Fort Bourgogne — the strongpoint the AFFS calls impregnable and the Capellans have twice proven is not. Twice in the old wars McCarron's Armored Cavalry crossed the Stannic Bridge — that three-mile span of Star League lostech nobody on either side will destroy — and cracked the fort's walls. The March rebuilt it stronger each time. Now, in the ilClan war, the Confederation has come to try a third.

A Capellan raiding column is down on the Saginaw plain and driving for the bridge, aiming to be over it and into Fort Bourgogne before the March can concentrate. The Marlette militia is stretched thin holding the capital at Achemar, so its commander hires your command for the one job that matters: hold the Stannic Bridge and the ground before the fort. The bridge itself is off both sides' target list — the Capellans want it whole to cross, and the Suns will not blow their own lostech — so it becomes exactly what a fortress needs, a single hard road the enemy has to force in the open.

This is a House contract with a fortress-world's pride behind it. Command is AFFS House, the wrecks are the March's, and the Marlette militia will remember whether Fort Bourgogne held on your watch or fell for a third time. Break the raid at the bridge and the Confederation goes home with nothing; let them across, and you are the mercenaries who did what even McCarron only managed twice.

contract.constraints: Command House (an AFFS militia liaison rides with you). Salvage Exchange (the March claims Capellan wrecks; you take the cash). The Stannic Bridge is off-limits to destruction by contract — a Star League lostech artifact.
contract.additionalRequirements: Track Scale 2; minimum fielded force 5,000 BV / 200 PV.
contract.bonus: Hold the fort — keep Fort Bourgogne across both tracks and the March grants +1 Reputation and battle-loss compensation (75% SP replacement) on any 'Mech lost at the bridge. Save it in rubble (Fortress Scars 3+) and the compensation is withheld.

missionBrief.behindScenes: A fortress-world defense with a preserved chokepoint. Track 1 is the bridge defense; the Track 1 result drives the branch. SUCCESS recoils the raid and you counter-strike its staging (t2a, Strike). FAILURE lets the Capellans onto the walls (t2b, Pushback to retake Fort Bourgogne). The tree ends after Track 2.

complications.effect: None.
Bern in flood. The river runs high — the near-bank low hexes become Level 1 water for 3 turns (Piloting checks to move through).
Militia sortie. A Marlette militia lance (two mediums, or a vehicle element; regular, Gunnery 4 / Piloting 5) sallies from the fort to join you.
Warrior House challenge. The Capellan commander calls out your commander for single combat on the bridge; win it for +1 Reputation, decline at no cost.
Fortress guns. Fort Bourgogne's artillery ranges the far bank — you get one free Battlefield Support artillery strike this track.
Roll twice, ignore repeats.

missionBrief.contractVictory: You: hold Fort Bourgogne — win the bridge in Track 1 and win Track 2. Capellan Confederation: take the fortress (force the bridge in Track 1, or hold the walls in Track 2b).
missionBrief.tally: Fortress Scars — each Fort Bourgogne structure destroyed (by anyone) across the contract counts 1. At 3+, the fort is saved in ruins: -1 Reputation and no battle-loss compensation.

namedCharacters.name: Sang-shao Lian Cho
namedCharacters.rule: Leads the raid in the McCarron tradition — bold at the bridge, and he will not destroy the Stannic span. If killed, the Capellan force is -2 Initiative for the rest of that track (Commander rule).

missionBrief.purchaseOptions: Between tracks, an AFFS Crucis March list — light/medium 'Mechs and combat vehicles, 2D6 of 8+. No assaults.

tracks.name: The Stannic Bridge
tracks.situation:
The Stannic Bridge is three and a half miles of Star League stonework across the Bern River, and it is the only fast way onto the plateau where Fort Bourgogne stands. The Capellan column has to force it in the open — the bridge is too valuable to drop, so there is no blowing it and no clever flank, just the span, the river, and the guns on both banks. You hold the near bank and the bridgehead; the Confederation has to come to you.

A defense is a clock, and the clock is the March relief massing at Achemar. Trade the far-bank approaches for time, keep the Capellans from establishing on your side of the Bern, and the relief arrives to a bridge still held. Break, and a Capellan armored regiment is loose on the road to a fortress that has fallen twice before.
tracks.deployment: Short edges, river map (the Bern River splits the field; the Stannic Bridge is the only crossing, at center — an intact multi-hex structure neither side may destroy). You (Defender) hold one-third of your force off-map (arriving end of Turn 1, own half); the rest sets up within 6 hexes of your home (near-bank) edge (12" AS; 12/18" at Scale 2+). The Capellan Confederation (Attacker) enters the far-bank edge Turn 1.

objectives.text: Hold the Bridgehead — half your force within 4 hexes of the near-bank bridge mouth at end of Turn 3 (6/12" Turn 4 at Scale 2+).
Bar the Bridge — no Capellan unit exits your home (fort-side) edge through end of Turn 6.
Force the Crossing — exit 3 units off the fort-side edge by end of Turn 6.
Overpower — more non-crippled BV/PV on the near bank at track end.

tracks.specialRules: The Stannic Bridge may not be destroyed by either side (Suns lostech / Capellan intent). A unit forced off the bridge into the Bern takes deep-water rules (Level 2+; risk of immobilization).
tracks.trackEnd: End of Turn 6 (Turn 8 AS at Scale 2+).
tracks.salvagePolicy: Winner-all (the March claims Capellan wrecks; SP at your salvage %).

forks.trigger: The bridge held; the Capellan column has recoiled to its staging ground on the Saginaw plain.
forks.consequence: Counter-strike their staging before they can refit and try the fort again.

forks.trigger: The Capellans forced the bridge and are onto the walls of Fort Bourgogne.
forks.consequence: Push them back out of the fortress before it falls for a third time.

tracks.name: Break Their Staging
tracks.situation:
The bridge held, and the Capellan column has recoiled to its staging ground on the Saginaw plain — a laager of supply and repair around the DropShip that brought them. A raid that lifts intact is a raid that comes back; the Marlette commander wants the Confederation taught that Fort Bourgogne costs more than it is worth. You go in to wreck their staging before they can refit.

A strike is about the target, not the ground. Get to the laager, put down the fuel and the repair gantries, and pull back before the Capellan rear guard can pin you; the point is the damage, not the field. Burn their staging and the raid is finished for this campaign; leave it standing, and Marlette sees them again before the season turns.
tracks.deployment: Long edges, open plain. The Capellan Confederation (Defender) sets up before Initiative in its own half, its guard around four objective structures near center — three supply and repair gantries (Medium buildings) and one fuel dump. One structure is secretly recorded as the DropShip fuel bladder. You (Attacker) enter half your force on your home edge Turn 1, the rest from a short edge Turn 2.

objectives.text: Case the Laager — scan 2 structures, or find the fuel bladder.
Screen the Staging — keep half your force within reach of the structures through Turn 4.
Fire the Gantries — destroy 2 of the supply/repair structures.
Blow the Bladder — identify and destroy the fuel bladder.
Hold the Field — keep half your force on the laager at track end.

tracks.specialRules: Scanning follows Strike reveal rules (a scanned structure's role becomes known; the fuel bladder can be identified). When the fuel bladder is destroyed, every unit within 2 hexes takes 10 damage (AS 2).
tracks.trackEnd: Default.
tracks.salvagePolicy: Pool-draft (Capellan wrecks to the March; SP at your salvage %).

forks.trigger: The staging is burned, or the Capellans hold it.
forks.consequence: Contract closes — tally Fortress Scars and settle the March's favor.

tracks.name: The Fort Bourgogne Walls
tracks.situation:
The Capellans forced the bridge, and now there is fighting on the walls of Fort Bourgogne itself — Confederation 'Mechs among the ramparts the March swore could never be taken a third time. This is the nightmare the militia hired you to prevent, and there is no time for finesse: every turn the Capellans hold the walls is a turn closer to the propaganda coup of a Davion fortress in Liao hands. You go in to put them back over the wall.

A pushback is a grind through prepared ground. You drive the Capellans back out of the fortress works, retaking the ramparts and gatehouses hex by hex while the walls channel the fight into short, brutal exchanges. Push them out past the outer wall and Fort Bourgogne stands for a third war; stall inside, and the fortress falls with your name on the report.
tracks.deployment: Long edges, fortress map (walls, gatehouses, and rampart buildings channel movement and block line of sight). The Capellan Confederation (Defender) sets up holding the inner works (within 6 hexes of center, among Heavy buildings). You (Attacker) enter from your home edge Turn 1 and push into and through the fortress.

objectives.text: Retake the Works — more of your non-crippled BV/PV within 3 hexes of the fortress center at end of Turn 4.
Hold the Walls — keep half your force in the fortress for 3 consecutive turns.
Drive Them Out — push 75% of the Capellan force back across the outer wall and out by Turn 10.
Hold a Gatehouse — keep one marked gatehouse Capellan-held at track end.
Make Them Bleed — destroy or cripple half the enemy force.

tracks.specialRules: Fortress buildings are Heavy. Each Fort Bourgogne structure destroyed (by anyone) adds to Fortress Scars.
tracks.trackEnd: Turn 10 (Turn 8 AS), or no Capellan 'Mechs left in the fortress.
tracks.salvagePolicy: Winner-all (the March claims; SP at your salvage %).

forks.trigger: The walls are cleared, or the fortress falls.
forks.consequence: Contract closes — tally Fortress Scars and settle what the March owes.

hotspots.title: The Barlow Line
hotspots.employer: Draconis March — deniable liberation op (AFFS + the Folly partisans)

a.employer: Draconis March — deniable liberation op (AFFS + the Folly partisans)

contract.constraints: Command Liaison (a partisan runner coordinates; no House officer commands your line). Deniable — no AFFS colors, no formal battle-loss comp; the March pays quietly and remembers.

a.situation: The Trinity Mountains are full of people waiting for a reason, and the March is sending them one. Slip into the peaks, link up with the Folly partisans, and break the Ryuken garrison's grip on Sparkle where it will hurt the legend most. No AFFS colors and no formal backing — only the oldest name in the Reach, waiting to be lit again.

b.employer: Draconis Combine — DCMS Ryuken-ni garrison (Chu-sa Toshiro Abe, out of Sparkle)

contract.constraints: Command House (a Ryuken garrison order). The Folly rises every generation — hold Sparkle and the mountain approaches, and claim the partisan iron.
contract.additionalRequirements: Track Scale 2; minimum fielded force 4,500 BV / 180 PV.
contract.bonus: Keep the Dragon's grip — hold Barlow's Folly and put the Sparkle uprising down and the Combine grants +1 Reputation and a garrison's salvage share of the mountain wrecks.

b.blurb: Hold Barlow's Folly for the Dragon — smother the Sparkle uprising and drive the outland raiders back into the peaks before the Folly's fire spreads across the Reach.
b.situation: Barlow's Folly rises every generation, and every generation the Dragon puts it down; Chu-sa Abe does not intend to be the exception. Outland raiders are somewhere on the Folly and the partisans are stirring toward Sparkle. Hold the capital, smother the rising before it catches, and drive the hired iron back into the snow.

hotspots.blurb: The Combine holds Barlow's Folly, the world whose fourteen-year resistance the Dragon could never fully kill. Flank the Ryuken garrison through the Trinity Mountains and light the fire again.
hotspots.regionNote: Canonical Draconis Reach world — conquered and garrisoned by the DCMS Ryuken-ni; Combine-held in 3151. A legitimate Draconis March / Reach entry.
hotspots.situation:
Every world in the Reach has a story; Barlow's Folly is a story the Combine could not finish. Three and a half centuries ago, when the Dragon overran this stretch of the Draconis March, one AFFS colonel — Michael Barlow, a native son — refused the retreat order and took his battalion into the Trinity Mountains that ring the world's three cities. For fourteen years he and his people raided out of those snow-capped peaks, and long after the last of them fell, the name kept fighting: 'Barlow's Folly' became a talisman for insurgents, a spirit of resistance so stubborn the Combine itself gave up and adopted the name.

In the ilClan war the Dragon took the Reach again, and a battered DCMS Ryuken regiment now garrisons Barlow's Folly out of the capital, Sparkle. But the old habit — a rifle by the door, a spare plate at the table — never died, and the Trinity Mountains are full of partisans waiting for a reason. The Draconis March means to give them one. It cannot spare a regiment for a deniable border world, so it hires your command to be that reason: slip into the mountains, link with the Folly partisans, and hit the Ryuken garrison where it will hurt the legend most.

The nuance is a job with no flag on it. This is a deniable liberation raid — command is loose, the partisans are your guides and your responsibility, and your reputation rides on whether Barlow's Folly rises or bleeds. Come out of the mountains hard, break the garrison's grip on Sparkle, and the whole Reach hears that the Folly stood up again; get caught in the open by a Ryuken that knows this ground, and you are the outlanders who spent a legend and left.

contract.constraints: Command Liaison (a partisan runner coordinates; no House officer commands your line). Deniable — no AFFS colors, no formal battle-loss comp; the March pays quietly and remembers.
contract.additionalRequirements: Track Scale 2; minimum fielded force 4,500 BV / 180 PV. Mobile / jump-capable designs favored (mountain ground).
contract.bonus: Raise the Folly — break the garrison's hold on Sparkle and the March grants +1 Reputation with the Draconis March and a partisan cache (a salvaged 'Mech from the mountains, one recovery-table roll) at contract end.

missionBrief.behindScenes: A mountain liberation raid. Track 1 is the flank through the Trinity Mountains; the Track 1 result drives the branch. SUCCESS lights the uprising in Sparkle (t2a, Objective Raid on the garrison). FAILURE compromises the raid and you cover the partisans back into the peaks (t2b, Retreat). Tree ends after Track 2.

complications.effect: None.
The mountains bite. Snow and rock — any 'Mech that runs or jumps in a hill/woods hex makes a Piloting check or slips (fall, no damage, prone).
Partisan guides. You know the ground: place one of your units anywhere on the map at setup (a mountain path only the Folly knows).
Ryuken honor. The garrison fights hard for its dead; the enemy commander will not retreat while any Ryuken 'Mech stands (no withdrawal).
Reprisal risk. Any civilian structure in Sparkle you destroy is a -1 Reputation flag (the partisans will pay for it).
Roll twice, ignore repeats.

missionBrief.contractVictory: You: break the Ryuken's hold — win the flank in Track 1 and win Track 2. Draconis Combine: hold Barlow's Folly (win Track 1, or hold the garrison in Track 2a).
missionBrief.tally: Reprisals — each Sparkle civilian structure destroyed (by anyone) across the contract counts 1. At 3+, the Dragon's reprisals fall on the Folly: -1 Reputation and no partisan cache.

namedCharacters.name: Chu-sa Toshiro Abe

tracks.name: Into the Trinity Mountains
tracks.situation:
The Ryuken garrison expects trouble on the roads to Sparkle, not out of the peaks behind it. So you come the way Barlow came — up through the Trinity Mountains, along paths the partisans have kept secret for three centuries, to fall on the garrison's flank where it is not looking. The mountains are your cover and your enemy both: rock, snow, and forest that hide you and slow you in equal measure.

A flank is about getting your weight onto the enemy's exposed side before it can turn to face you. Come down out of the high ground onto the Ryuken's flank, break their line before they can re-form, and the road to Sparkle opens. Get strung out on the climb and caught mid-descent, and a garrison that knows this ground will pin you against the peaks.

Face the Threat — the Combine turns half its force to engage your flank within 2 turns.

Open the Road — exit 3 units off the Combine's home (Sparkle) edge.

tracks.name: The Sparkle Uprising
tracks.situation:
The flank landed, and Sparkle is in the streets — three centuries of banked resentment lit in a single night. The Ryuken garrison is falling back on its strongpoints: the government house, the militia armory, the spaceport control. Take those from them while the city has its blood up, and the Combine's hold on Barlow's Folly is finished; leave them, and the reprisals will put the fire out for another generation.

An objective raid is a smash-and-grab against the clock. Reach the marked strongpoints, take or wreck them before the Ryuken can consolidate, and let the partisans hold what you break. Every strongpoint that falls is a piece of the garrison's grip; every one that holds is a place the Dragon rallies.
tracks.deployment: Long edges, urban map. The Draconis Combine (Defender) sets up within 6 hexes of center around three strongpoint structures (Medium buildings — government house, armory, spaceport control). You (Attacker) enter Turn 1; partisan mobs (immobile objective markers) mark the risen districts.

Hold the Line — keep half your force within reach of the strongpoints through Turn 4.
Take the City — control (adjacent, no enemy adjacent) 2 of the 3 strongpoints at end of Turn 5.
Rally the Dragon — keep 2 of the 3 strongpoints Combine-held at end of Turn 5.
Bloody the Garrison — destroy or cripple half the Ryuken force.

tracks.trackEnd: End of Turn 8, or all strongpoints resolved.

forks.consequence: Contract closes — tally Reprisals and settle the March's quiet favor.

tracks.name: Back to the Peaks
tracks.situation:
The Ryuken knew this ground better than the partisans hoped, and the raid is blown — the garrison is between you and the mountains, and the reprisal squads are already moving on the villages that helped you. The job now is the oldest one on Barlow's Folly: get the fighters back into the Trinity Mountains alive, so the legend lives to rise another day.

A retreat is a fighting withdrawal, not a rout. You cover the partisan column as it climbs for the peaks, trading the foothills for the minutes they need to disappear into the rock and snow. Get them into the mountains and the Folly keeps its fire banked; let the Ryuken catch them in the open, and three centuries of resistance end in one afternoon.

Break Contact — exit at least one partisan marker off the mountain edge.
