Move quiet, stay unfound, and reach Cartago city before the Suns' hired hunters can fix your line of march. The gravity punishes haste — so does being seen.

hotspots.blurb: A Combine column is down somewhere in Cartago's high-gravity jungle, and nobody knows where. Find it before it finds the capital — on a world that punishes every misstep.
hotspots.situation:
Cartago is a hard world to fight on and a harder one to fight for. It sits far out from a white F-class sun — seventeen days' sail from the jump point — five steaming continents of high-gravity jungle where the air presses heavy and the equator runs to forty-two degrees. At a quarter again Terran gravity, everything is slower and everything is heavier: 'Mechs bog in the wet, heat sinks lose the race, and a pilot who forgets where he is finds the ground coming up fast. The Federated Suns holds it because it anchors the Robinson approaches, and because the Combine keeps testing to see if the Suns still can.

This is one of those tests. A Combine raiding column jumped in-system and dropped somewhere on the Paraíso continent, and in that jungle 'somewhere' is a real problem — the canopy blinds sensors, the heat blinds thermals, and a column that stays quiet can move a long way before anyone sees it. The AFFS garrison at Cartago city is too thin to picket the whole coast, so its commander hires your command for the job the regulars can't cover: find the Combine before it finds the capital, and hit it while it is still strung out in the green.

The nuance is a House contract fought against the clock and the climate. Command is AFFS House, the wrecks are the March's, and the high gravity is a third army that does not care whose side you are on. Find the column early and you fight it on your terms in the open; find it late, and you are fighting it at the gates of Cartago city with a garrison's worth of civilians behind you.

contract.constraints: Command House (an AFFS liaison rides with you). Salvage Exchange (the March claims Combine wrecks; you take the cash). High-gravity rules are in force all contract (see complications).

missionBrief.behindScenes: A recon-in-force on a high-gravity world. Track 1 is the search of the Paraíso jungle; the Track 1 result drives the branch. SUCCESS finds the column early and forces an open fight (t2a, Meeting Engagement). FAILURE loses it in the green and it reaches the capital (t2b, Defend Cartago city). The tree ends after Track 2.

complications.effect: High-g baseline (always on): running/jumping costs +1 heat that turn, and any Piloting check to avoid a fall is at -1 (the ground is unforgiving).
Monsoon. The jungle floods — low hexes become Level 1 water for 3 turns; Piloting checks to move through.
Local scouts. Cartago rangers feed you intel: scan (reveal) one enemy unit for free at the start of the track.
Canopy blackout. Spotting beyond 6 hexes fails on a 1-2 (1D6) for the first 3 turns (the green swallows sensors).
Heat exhaustion. Any 'Mech that ends a turn at 10+ heat takes a -1 to-hit next turn (the air won't cool it).
Roll twice, ignore repeats.

missionBrief.contractVictory: You: spoil the raid — win the search in Track 1 and win Track 2. Draconis Combine: reach and take the capital (evade in Track 1, or take Cartago city in Track 2b).

namedCharacters.name: Tai-i Rina Fujimoto

tracks.name: Reading the Jungle
tracks.situation:
The column is out there in the Paraíso green, and the only way to find it is to go looking — a screen of your fastest machines sweeping the coast, reading the trampled canopy and the cold spots the heat can't hide. Every hour you spend blind is an hour the Combine gets closer to the capital; every enemy machine you tag is a piece of the puzzle of where they are going.

A recon is about knowledge, not ground. Scan the column, learn its weight and its heading, and get that word back to Cartago city before you are seen — or, if the chance comes, blood their point element and force them to show their hand. Read them early and the next fight is on your terms; miss them, and the first anyone sees of the Combine is the smoke over the capital.
tracks.deployment: The Attacker (you, roll or bid) picks any edge first; the Defender (Combine) takes any other. The Combine sets up anywhere with at least half its force in the half nearest you; you enter Turn 1. High-gravity rules in force.

objectives.text: Scan the Column — scan (identify) 1 enemy unit per scale.
Stay Hidden — keep half your force off the enemy's scans for 2 turns.
Read Them Cold — scan two-thirds of the Combine force.
Slip the Screen — exit half the Combine force off the far (capital) edge unscanned.
First Blood — first side to destroy or cripple 25% of the enemy scores it.

tracks.trackEnd: Turn 8 (Turn 8 AS).
tracks.salvagePolicy: Pool-draft (wrecks pooled, alternate picks, winner first).

forks.trigger: You read the column early and caught it strung out in the open.
forks.consequence: Force the fight now, in the open, before they can reach the capital.

forks.trigger: The column slipped your screen in the green and is at the gates of Cartago city.
forks.consequence: Fall back and hold the capital against a raid you never got to size up.

tracks.name: Meet Them in the Open
tracks.situation:
You found the column before it found cover, and now the Combine has to fight where you caught it — a clearing on the Paraíso coast, both forces coming onto open ground with the jungle at their backs. This is the fight the search was for: no walls, no capital behind you, just weight against weight on ground you chose.

A meeting engagement is decided by who seizes the center first and holds it. Get your force onto the clearing and break the Combine line before it can pull back into the green, and the raid dies here in the open. Let them reach the treeline and it becomes a hunt through the canopy you cannot afford.
tracks.deployment: Short edges, coastal clearing. Both forces enter Turn 1 from opposite home edges; neither sets up in advance. The center of the clearing is the contested ground. High-gravity rules in force.

objectives.text: Seize the Clearing — more of your non-crippled BV/PV in the center third than the enemy at end of Turn 4.
Hold the Ground — the same at end of Turn 8.
Break the Column — reduce the Combine to half its starting BV/PV (tie = neither).
Commander's Fall — destroy the enemy commander's unit.

tracks.trackEnd: Default (Turn 10 / Turn 8 AS, or one side has no 'Mechs).
tracks.salvagePolicy: Winner-all (the March claims Combine wrecks; SP at your salvage %).

forks.consequence: Contract closes — settle the March's favor and the spoiled-raid bonus.

tracks.name: Hold the Capital
tracks.situation:
The column slipped the screen, and the first Cartago city knew of it was a Combine 'Mech on the ring road. There is no time to be clever now — the raid is at the gates, and behind you is a capital full of people who trusted the garrison to see this coming. You hold the approaches and buy the city the time it needs.

A defense is a clock, and the clock is the AFFS relief moving up from the spaceport. Trade the outer districts for the minutes they need, keep the Combine off the government quarter, and the relief arrives to a capital that stood. Break, and the raid gets exactly the prize it crossed seventeen days of space for.
tracks.deployment: Short edges, city-approach map. You (Defender) hold one-third of your force off-map (arriving end of Turn 1, own half); the rest sets up within 6 hexes of your home edge (12" AS; 12/18" at Scale 2+), the government quarter (objective) at center. The Draconis Combine (Attacker) enters Turn 1. High-gravity rules in force.

Bar the Gate — no Combine unit adjacent to the government quarter through end of Turn 6.

tracks.trackEnd: End of Turn 6 (Turn 8 AS at Scale 2+).

Get around it on the open flats and run it down before it reaches its DropShips. A picture that reaches Ishara cannot be taken back.

b.blurb: Run Ishara's forward edge under Sho-sa Tomoe — read the PDZ's guns at Fort Mason and carry the picture home before the Suns' hired guns can shut your road to the ships.
b.situation: Tai-shu Ishara's storm opens where Sho-sa Tomoe says it opens, and she is on Le Blanc to find out. Read Fort Mason — the headquarters, the guard, the ground — and carry the picture home across the border. The flats are open and the Suns will hire speed to shut your road to the ships; finish the work before they close it.

hotspots.blurb: The Combine offensive everyone feared has a forward edge, and it just showed up on the Le Blanc mining flats. Run it down before it reads the March's throat and jumps out with what it saw.
hotspots.situation:
Le Blanc is a rock with just enough air to breathe, a mining world of thin atmosphere and arid flats where the food is imported and the only real industry is digging. It matters far past its size, because since the Kentares Massacre the Armed Forces of the Federated Suns have run the Kentares prefecture from Fort Mason here — this dust-colored world is the ear the March keeps pressed to the Combine border, and a hiring hall old enough that mercenaries still drift in looking for a wage. Right now the wage is dangerous, because the storm the March has been bracing for has finally put a scout on the ground.

A Draconis Combine deep-recon element — fast, careful, and clearly the forward edge of something much larger — jumped in and dropped onto the ore flats outside Fort Mason. It is not here to take the world. It is here to read it: to fix the PDZ headquarters, count what defends it, and carry that picture back to the officer whose offensive it opens. Prisoners and intercepts give that officer a name your command will learn to hate before this is over — Tai-shu Genji Ishara, Warlord of the border, and the machine on the flats belongs to his spearhead. Let it finish its work and jump out, and the first blow of the whole campaign lands with the March's guard already mapped.

The contract is a House job with the PDZ's own liaison at your shoulder: get around the recon element on the open flats, run it down before it reaches its DropShips, and take whatever it has learned off the board with it. Fort Mason's own thin garrison holds the headquarters if you fail — but a picture that reaches Ishara is a picture that cannot be taken back.

SUCCESS gets you around the scout and into a running fight (t2a, Pursuit). FAILURE lets it reach Fort Mason's approaches (t2b, Defend). Both branches converge on Track 3 (Recon), the fight to strip the intel off the wreck before it uploads. Sho-sa Tomoe recurs in hs-drm-20 and hs-drm-21 and pays off at the Mallory capstone.

tracks.name: Around the Ore Flats
tracks.situation:
The scout is running the open flats between the tailing fields and its landing zone, keeping to the low ground where the dust hides it and the sensors are thin. The straight chase is the losing move — it will see you coming and simply lead you in a circle until its uplink is done. The win is to get around it: swing wide through the workings, cut the line between the scout and its ships, and be standing on its road home before it knows you left Fort Mason.

A flank is a race you win before the shooting starts. Read the ground, spend the movement, and close the back door — get enough of your force behind the Combine element and it has to fight its way through you instead of jumping out clean. Leave the door open and it slides past into the running fight on its own terms.
tracks.deployment: Long edges, open flats with scattered level-1 tailings. You (Attacker) may split your force and enter from your home edge and one flank edge (declare before setup); the Combine (Defender) sets up centered, moving toward the far/landing edge. You enter Turn 1. Thin-air rules in force.

objectives.text: Close the Back Door — end Turn 4 with units totaling half your BV/PV between the Combine force and the far (landing) edge.
Keep Running — exit or hold half the scout force toward the landing edge by Turn 6.
Cut Them Off — no Combine unit reaches within 6 hexes of the landing edge through Turn 6.
Break Contact — get two-thirds of the scout force off the landing edge.
Draw Blood — first side to cripple or destroy 25% of the enemy scores it.

tracks.trackEnd: Turn 8 (Turn 8 AS).
tracks.salvagePolicy: Pool-draft (wrecks pooled, alternate picks, winner first).

forks.trigger: You got behind the scout and shut its road home.
forks.consequence: Run it down in the open before it can reach its ships.

forks.trigger: The scout slipped your flank and is pushing on Fort Mason's approaches.
forks.consequence: Fall back and screen the PDZ headquarters while it finishes its read.

tracks.name: Run Them to the Ships
tracks.situation:
You are on its road home and it knows it — the scout has thrown off the careful reconnaissance and is running flat-out for its DropShips, shedding the slow to save the fast. This is the moment the whole contract turns on: catch the command element on the flats and Ishara's first picture of the March dies with it; let it reach the ramps and it carries everything you tried to stop.

A pursuit is a knife-fight at speed. Push your fastest onto the runners, force the Piloting checks that spill a machine at a dead run, and above all put fire on the command 'Mech — Tomoe will spend every one of her own to buy it clear. Cripple or take her and the data goes nowhere.
tracks.deployment: Short edges, same-edge start (both from your Track-1 pursuit edge). The Combine (Defender, quarry) enters Turn 1 running for the far (landing) edge; half its force must have a maximum move of 8 or less (16" AS) — the slow it could not shed. You (Attacker) enter Turn 2. Thin-air rules in force.

objectives.text: Run Them Down — destroy or immobilize half the fleeing Combine BV/PV before it exits.
Make the Ramps — exit half your BV/PV off the landing edge by Turn 10.
Take the Picture — destroy or capture the command element (Tomoe's unit) before it exits.
Carry It Clear — exit the command element off the landing edge.
No Prisoners of the Data — prevent any Combine unit from exiting for a full turn after Turn 6.

tracks.specialRules: A Combine unit that exits the landing edge is removed (escaped, not destroyed). If Tomoe's unit exits, the Combine scores the contract's intelligence objective.
tracks.trackEnd: Turn 10 (Turn 8 AS), or the Combine force has exited/been destroyed.
tracks.salvagePolicy: Attacker-only-if-win (you claim the flats' wrecks; SP at your salvage %).

forks.trigger: The chase is settled on the flats — the wreck field, and its data core, are yours to reach.
forks.consequence: Get to the downed scout and strip its intel before it uploads or self-wipes.

tracks.name: Screen Fort Mason
tracks.situation:
The scout slipped your flank, and now it is doing on Fort Mason's doorstep exactly what it came to do — sitting off the headquarters at range, reading the PDZ's guns and gates while you scramble back to chase it off. You cannot let it work unhurt. Every minute it holds that overwatch is another line in Ishara's picture.

A screen is a spoiler, not a wall — you do not have to destroy the scout, only make it flinch, break its firing lines, and drive it off its overwatch before it finishes. Push it back off the headquarters approaches and the picture goes home incomplete; let it sit, and the March's throat is mapped.
tracks.deployment: Short edges, Fort Mason approach map. You (Defender) set up within 8 hexes of your home edge (16" AS), the headquarters and its overwatch ridge (objectives) toward center; one-third of your force arrives end of Turn 1 (own half). The Combine (Attacker) enters Turn 1 and seeks the overwatch ground. Thin-air rules in force.

objectives.text: Break the Overwatch — no Combine unit holds the overwatch ridge (center) at end of Turn 4.
Hold the Ridge — a Combine unit on the overwatch ridge at end of Turn 4.
Drive Them Off — no Combine unit within 8 hexes of the headquarters through end of Turn 6.
Finish the Read — keep a spotting unit with line of sight to the headquarters for any 4 turns.
Bloody Nose — cripple or destroy the enemy commander's unit (Tomoe).

tracks.specialRules: A Combine unit with unbroken line of sight to the headquarters hex accrues the read; four turns of read (any units, cumulative) completes the Combine's intelligence objective for this track.
tracks.trackEnd: End of Turn 6 (Turn 8 AS).
tracks.salvagePolicy: Defender-only-if-win (you claim what falls near the HQ; SP at your salvage %).

forks.trigger: The scout is driven off the HQ, or it finished its read and pulled back to its ships.
forks.consequence: Chase the withdrawing element to its landing site and take the data before it uploads.

tracks.name: The Data Core
tracks.situation:
It comes down to a wreck and a countdown. The scout's command machine is down on the flats near its landing site, its crew fighting to upload the reconnaissance to the waiting DropShip — or to wipe it before you can pull it — while the last of the Combine force forms a shell around it. What you carry off this field decides whether Ishara opens his war blind or with the March's guard drawn out for him.

A recon-to-recover is a race with teeth: punch a lane to the downed core, hold the ground around it long enough for the PDZ's specialists to strip it, and keep any Combine unit from reaching the uplink or the ships with a copy. Take the core intact and you have Ishara's own plan in your hands; lose it and the storm still opens on his timing.
tracks.deployment: Short edges, landing-site map; the downed core (objective) sits in a central clearing. You (Attacker) enter Turn 1. The Combine (Defender) sets up within 4 hexes of the core, a shell around it, with the landing edge (its DropShip) behind. Thin-air rules in force.

objectives.text: Reach the Core — a unit of yours ends a turn adjacent to the core with no Combine unit adjacent.
Hold the Shell — a Combine unit adjacent to the core, none of yours, at end of Turn 4.
Strip It Clean — hold the core (adjacent, no enemy adjacent) for two full turns; the specialists pull the data.
Send a Copy — exit any Combine unit off the landing edge after Turn 3 (a courier reaches the ship).
Take the Blade — destroy or capture Tomoe's unit on this field.

tracks.specialRules: If the Combine holds the core adjacent (no attacker adjacent) at the end of any two turns, the crew wipes it (neither side scores the intelligence). Stripping it clean or an exited Combine courier resolves the contract's intelligence objective for whoever achieves theirs first.
tracks.trackEnd: End of Turn 8 (Turn 8 AS), or the core is stripped/wiped.
tracks.salvagePolicy: Winner-all (the March claims Combine wrecks; SP at your salvage %).

forks.trigger: The core is stripped, wiped, or a copy reached the ships.
forks.consequence: Contract closes — settle the PDZ's favor and, if you took the picture off the board, the priority-resupply credit. Word of Tai-shu Ishara's spearhead goes up the chain.

b.blurb: Hold Ishara's muster at New Derry under Tomoe — the fuel and stores that open the storm — and pin the deniable raiders on Galtor before they can burn the offensive's edge.
b.situation: The stores outside New Derry open the Warlord's storm, and Sho-sa Tomoe holds their near guard. A deniable strike force is coming — no flags, no support, a long way from home. Keep the muster intact, pin the raiders on Galtor's jungle ground, and the offensive jumps on schedule with their wrecks in its train.

hotspots.blurb: Ishara is massing his offensive on Galtor III, across the line in Combine space. The March can't be seen there — but you can. Wreck his staging before it jumps, and get out clean.
hotspots.regionNote: Galtor III is a Draconis Combine world across the FS-DC border; this is a deniable cross-border raid (AFFS off the books). Profile figures are Sarna-sourced; the population is the last printed figure (3079).
hotspots.situation:
Galtor is a name the Federated Suns remembers — a hot, wet jungle world of three green continents around a white sun, where a Davion army once broke a Combine offensive so badly the campaign got its own name. In the ilClan years the border has moved and Galtor III flies the Dragon's flag, and the Warlord Genji Ishara has chosen the old battlefield for a fitting purpose: it is where he is massing the offensive that opened on Le Blanc. Muster fields, fuel, and forward stores are stacking up outside New Derry, waiting for the order to jump at the March.

The March cannot answer that openly. To be seen fighting on a Combine world is to hand the Dragon the excuse for the very war Ishara is preparing. So the answer is you — a deniable strike, no flags, no liaison, off every book the AFFS keeps. Robinson's operational staff will get you across the line and leave you there; what you do to Ishara's staging is your own, and so is getting home. Hit the muster hard enough and the offensive loses the weeks it takes to rebuild it; that is weeks the March buys to ready its own defense.

The contract is a raider's bargain. Command is Independent — you answer to no one on the ground because officially you were never there — the pay runs high for the risk, and the salvage split is a raider's share of whatever you can drag home. Standing over it all is Ishara's spearhead, back from Le Blanc: Sho-sa Kaede Tomoe holds the muster's near guard, and she has learned your command's face.

contract.constraints: Command Independent (deniable — no liaison, no flags; officially you were never on Galtor). Straight/70 support. Transport 50% (you make your own way in and out). Salvage 30% (a raider keeps a good share of what it drags home).
contract.additionalRequirements: Track Scale 2; minimum fielded force 4,500 BV / 180 PV. A self-supporting strike force — heat-efficient designs favored (jungle, 45°C, standard gravity).
contract.bonus: Break the muster — destroy the forward stores in Track 2a (or hold the line long enough to burn them in 2b) and Robinson's staff quietly grants +1 Reputation and a 30% battle-loss credit on any 'Mech lost across the line (a raid that hurts the Dragon is worth paying for, off the books).

missionBrief.behindScenes: The middle of the Ishara thread — you take the war to his ground. Track 1 (Assault) is the landing and push onto the muster fields; the result drives the branch. SUCCESS breaks in and you go for the stores (t2a, Objective Raid). FAILURE gets pinned by Tomoe's counter and you fight to break contact (t2b, Breakthrough). Both branches converge on Track 3 (Meeting Engagement), the running clash at the extraction fields as you fight clear. Tomoe (Gunnery/Piloting improved from hs-drm-19) recurs at hs-drm-21.

complications.effect: Jungle heat (always on): any 'Mech that ends a turn at 8+ heat takes a -1 to-hit the next turn (45°C and no cooling to spare).
Canopy. Woods are heavier than they look — line of sight beyond 5 hexes through jungle is blocked (treat as heavy woods for spotting).
Stolen march. You caught the guard changing — one Combine unit deploys shut down (starts the track powered down; may restart normally).
River line. A jungle river crosses the field — one band of hexes is Level 1-2 water (Piloting to cross; depth by table).
Reinforced. Ishara's muster is not asleep — the Combine gets one extra light or medium unit (GM's pick from the era list) entering end of Turn 2.
Roll twice, ignore repeats.

missionBrief.contractVictory: You: cripple the offensive — break the muster's forward stores (Track 2a) or burn them under fire (Track 2b), then fight clear in Track 3. Draconis Combine: save the muster and pin the raiders (hold the stores, or stop your force from extracting in Track 3).

namedCharacters.name: Sho-sa Kaede Tomoe
namedCharacters.rule: She has fought your command before and will not be flanked twice — she holds the near guard and counters toward your line of retreat. If her unit is destroyed or immobilized, the Combine force is -2 Initiative for the rest of that track (Commander).

namedCharacters.name: Colonel Sabine Marchetti
namedCharacters.role: Employer — AFFS Robinson operational staff (off the books)
namedCharacters.rule: Never appears on the ground; her interest is the delay you buy the March, not your survival — the deniability cuts both ways.

missionBrief.purchaseOptions: Between tracks (staged from the March side before you cross), an AFFS Robinson-district list — medium and heavy 'Mechs and fast combat vehicles, 2D6 of 8+. No fixed resupply on the ground: you carry what you crossed with.

tracks.name: The New Derry Muster
tracks.situation:
You come down in the green outside New Derry with the muster fields spread below you — rows of vehicles and stores and the guard that watches them, all lit by a white sun and steaming in the jungle heat. There is no subtlety left once your DropShips are seen; the only thing that matters now is to hit the muster hard and get onto it before the guard can set. Every minute you spend in the treeline is a minute Tomoe uses to form her line.

An assault is weight and will — punch through the near guard, take the muster's edge, and break the defenders' cohesion before they can wall you off from the stores. Get onto the fields and the raid is alive and the next move is yours; get held in the green and you are fighting Ishara's whole near guard on his ground, exactly the fight he wants.
tracks.deployment: Short edges, jungle-and-clearing map; the muster fields (objective ground) sit in the far third, the Combine (Defender) set up around them. You (Attacker) enter Turn 1 from the treeline. Jungle-heat rules in force.

objectives.text: Take the Edge — end Turn 4 with units totaling half your BV/PV in the muster's near third (the field edge).
Hold the Line — keep half the muster ground clear of attacker units at end of Turn 4.
Break the Guard — reduce the Combine near guard to half its starting BV/PV.
Wall Them Off — no attacker unit reaches the muster's central store rows through Turn 6.
First Onto the Field — first side to control (adjacent, no enemy adjacent) any store row scores it.

tracks.specialRules: The side that scores more VP here sets Track 2: winner picks home edge and forces the loser to deploy first.
tracks.trackEnd: Default (Turn 10 / Turn 8 AS, or one side has no 'Mechs).
tracks.salvagePolicy: Attacker-only-if-win (what you can drag off the field is yours; SP at your salvage %).

forks.trigger: You broke the near guard and stand on the muster's edge.
forks.consequence: Drive for the forward stores and put them to the torch before the Combine reforms.

forks.trigger: Tomoe's counter caught you short of the field and is closing the trap.
forks.consequence: Fight to break contact and salvage the raid before you are surrounded.

tracks.name: Burn the Stores
tracks.situation:
You are on the muster fields with the stores in reach — the fuel, the munitions, the stacked forward supply that turns Ishara's gathered units into an offensive. The guard is broken but not gone, and it knows exactly what you are here to do. This is the whole point of crossing the line: put the stores to the torch and the storm Ishara opened on Le Blanc loses the weeks it takes to gather them again.

A raid on stores is a race against reaction. Get demolition units onto the store rows, hold them the moment it takes to fire them, and do not let the Combine buy the rows back with a counter-rush. Every row you burn is a piece of the offensive that will not arrive; leave them and the guard reforms around a muster still ready to jump.
tracks.deployment: Short edges, muster-field map; the store rows (three objective clusters) run across the center. You (Attacker) enter Turn 1 (or hold your Track-1 ground per the VP winner). The Combine (Defender) sets up around the rows and counters in. Jungle-heat rules in force.

objectives.text: Fire a Row — control (adjacent, no defender adjacent) any store row at end of a turn; it burns.
Save the Stores — hold two of the three rows clear of attacker units at end of Turn 5.
Break the Muster — burn all three store rows.
Beat Them Off — retake (control) any burning row before it is fully fired (destroy the attacker holding it that turn).
Commander's Fall — destroy or capture Tomoe's unit on the field.

tracks.specialRules: A store row held for one full turn is fired (scored, removed from play). Burning rows throw smoke: adjacent hexes are treated as light woods for line of sight.
tracks.trackEnd: End of Turn 8 (Turn 8 AS), or all rows are fired.
tracks.salvagePolicy: None (this is a burn, not a haul; the fields are aflame — nothing recovered here, but the contract salvage % still applies to wrecks you tow off).

forks.trigger: The stores are burning, or the guard held enough of them — either way the Combine is fully roused and your ships are calling.
forks.consequence: Fight your way back to the extraction fields through everything Galtor can throw at you.

tracks.name: Break Contact
tracks.situation:
The assault stalled in the green and Tomoe read it exactly — her counter has your force half-surrounded short of the fields, and the trap is closing by the minute. There is no muster to burn from in here; there is only getting your command out with its teeth intact and something to show for the crossing. A raid that dies on the enemy's ground gives the Dragon a propaganda victory to go with the offensive.

A breakthrough is a hard shoulder and a chosen lane. Pick the weak seam in Tomoe's ring, mass on it, and drive through before the jaws meet — and if you can put a torch to the near stores as you pass, the crossing was not for nothing. Break clean and you still bought the March its weeks; get pinned and Galtor becomes the place your command ended.
tracks.deployment: Short edges, jungle map; you (Attacker) start in the center, partly encircled — the Combine (Defender) sets up in an arc between you and the far (extraction) edge. You break Turn 1 toward the extraction edge. Jungle-heat rules in force.

objectives.text: Punch Through — exit half your BV/PV off the far (extraction) edge by Turn 8.
Close the Jaws — destroy or hold in place half the raiding force short of the edge.
Bring Them Out — exit two-thirds of your force off the extraction edge.
Spring the Trap — reduce the raiders to half their starting BV/PV before they clear the edge.
Torch on the Way Out — control and fire one near store row as you pass (per 2a rules).

tracks.specialRules: A unit that exits the extraction edge is out (safe). Firing a near store row here still counts toward the contract's break-the-muster bonus.
tracks.trackEnd: End of Turn 8 (Turn 8 AS), or your force has exited/been destroyed.
tracks.salvagePolicy: None (a fighting withdrawal; contract salvage % applies only to wrecks you actually tow off the edge).

forks.trigger: You broke the ring, or paid to — the survivors are running for the ships.
forks.consequence: Fight the last clash at the extraction fields and get what is left of your command off Galtor.

tracks.name: The Extraction Fields
tracks.situation:
It ends where you came in — a stretch of cleared ground on the Samphire coast where your DropShips wait with their ramps down and the last of Ishara's roused guard coming on hard to stop you leaving. Both forces arrive onto the same open field with the same urgency: yours to get aboard and gone, the Combine's to keep you on their world long enough to finish you. Everything the raid did is banked only if your command flies off Galtor.

A meeting engagement at the ramps is a brawl with a clock. Hold the extraction ground, keep the lanes to the ships open, and break the guard's rush before it can pin your slow units in the open. Get aboard and the crossing was a victory Ishara will feel; get caught on the field, and the March's deniable strike becomes the Dragon's kill.
tracks.deployment: Short edges, coastal clearing with the extraction edge (your DropShips) at your back. Both forces enter Turn 1 from opposite home edges; neither sets up in advance. The center clearing is the contested lane. Jungle-heat rules in force.

objectives.text: Hold the Lane — more of your non-crippled BV/PV in the center third than the enemy at end of Turn 4.
Get Aboard — exit half your BV/PV off the extraction edge by Turn 8.
Keep Them on Galtor — hold half the raiders on the field (unexited) at end of Turn 8.
Break the Rush — reduce the Combine guard to half its starting BV/PV (tie = neither).
The Blade Again — destroy or cripple Tomoe's unit before you fly out.

tracks.specialRules: A unit that exits the extraction edge is aboard (safe, counts as survived for the contract). Tomoe fights to the field's end here — she does not withdraw.
tracks.trackEnd: Default (Turn 10 / Turn 8 AS, or one side has no 'Mechs).
tracks.salvagePolicy: Winner-all of the field (but you keep only what you can tow aboard before you lift; SP at your salvage %).

forks.trigger: Your command is aboard and lifting, or held on Galtor at the last.
forks.consequence: Contract closes — settle the deniable pay and, if you broke the muster, Robinson's quiet bonus. Ishara's offensive has bled; his spearhead has not forgotten you.

b.blurb: Hold Ishara's spearhead at New Pontiac under Tomoe — his blade, at her peak and done running — and keep the offensive's edge intact against the decapitation raid come to break it.
b.situation: The spearhead at New Pontiac is the edge of the whole offensive, and the Suns know it — a decapitation raid is coming for Sho-sa Tomoe and the units around her. She has been flanked at Le Blanc and burned at Galtor, and she is done running. Hold the assembly together until relief lands, and keep the storm's edge whole.

hotspots.blurb: Ishara's spearhead is staging one jump from the March at Marduk, and its commander has a name you know. Break the spear before it falls — and its blade may come looking for you.
hotspots.regionNote: Marduk is a Draconis Combine world across the border; a deep-strike raid at the edge of the offensive. Profile figures are Sarna-sourced; the population is the last printed figure (3079). This contract is the last regular Hot Spot on the Ishara thread before the Mallory / New Ivaarsen capstones.
hotspots.situation:
Marduk is a big, crowded world — three continents and better than two billion people under a heavy gold-white sun, close enough to its jump point that a force can be down in under a week. That nearness is why the Warlord Genji Ishara staged the tip of his offensive here: a fast, hard spearhead poised one short jump from the Draconis March, ready to lead the whole storm in. Bleed a muster on Galtor and the offensive slows; break the spearhead itself at Marduk and it loses the edge that was meant to open the door.

AFFS high command has decided that edge is worth a decapitation raid, and it has picked your command because you have already met the officer who holds it. Sho-sa Kaede Tomoe — Ishara's blade, the commander who read you at Fort Mason and held the muster on Galtor — leads the spearhead's assembly at New Pontiac. Take her and the units around her out of the offensive and Ishara loses the one subordinate he was counting on to carry the first blow. He will have to commit himself. That is the point.

This is a House job flown deep, with a high-command observer riding to see it done and the pay to match a raid that could end the offensive before it starts. But Tomoe has learned your command's face across two worlds, and a blade that has been flanked and burned is a blade with a grudge. Corner her and she may not run a third time — she may turn and offer the old Combine answer to a rival she respects: single combat, her machine against your best, the spearhead's honor against yours. However this ends, the storm that follows falls on Mallory's World, and the Reckoning after it will be the Warlord's own.

Whatever the result, completing this contract arms the campaign's endgame — the Reckoning at Mallory's World.

missionBrief.behindScenes: The last regular Hot Spot on the Ishara thread; it hands off to the capstones. Track 1 (Strike) is the descent on the New Pontiac assembly; its result drives the branch. SUCCESS scatters the guard and corners Tomoe, who answers with a challenge (t2a, Duel). FAILURE lets the spearhead rally and you fight to withdraw with what you broke (t2b, Retreat). Both branches converge on Track 3 (Assault), the final push to finish the assembly before Combine relief lands. Tomoe is at her peak here (Gunnery 2 / Piloting 3); this is her last stand before Ishara commits personally at the Mallory capstone.

complications.effect: Assembly alert (always on): the spearhead is forming, not resting — one Combine unit per lance may make a free facing change at the start of each of the first two turns (they were already mounting up).
City edge. New Pontiac's outskirts crowd the field — one band of hexes is light-building urban terrain (partial cover; collateral risk to Reputation if leveled).
The observer's eye. The high-command liaison flags a target — reveal (scan) Tomoe's unit and one other free at the start of the track.
Heavy sun. The G8 sun bakes the field — any 'Mech at 9+ heat at end of turn takes -1 to-hit next turn.
Relief inbound. Combine reaction forces are closer than hoped — a Combine reinforcement (GM's pick, one medium/heavy from the era list) enters end of Turn 3.
Roll twice, ignore repeats.

missionBrief.contractVictory: You: break the spear — beat or take Tomoe (Track 2a Duel or on the field) and reduce the spearhead's assembly below half in Track 3. Draconis Combine: keep the spearhead intact — save Tomoe and hold the assembly together until relief lands.

namedCharacters.name: Sho-sa Kaede Tomoe
namedCharacters.rule: At her peak and done running. If cornered (the Track-1 result gates the Duel branch), she issues a formal challenge to your best pilot: a duel while the fields burn around them. She fights to the end here. If her unit is destroyed or captured, the Combine assembly is -2 Initiative and may not voluntarily withdraw for the rest of the track (Commander); breaking her arms the campaign's endgame.

namedCharacters.name: Leftenant General Cort Vlahos
namedCharacters.role: Employer — AFFS Draconis March high command (observer)
namedCharacters.rule: Rides as the Liaison observer; his report decides whether the March believes the offensive can be met head-on at Mallory. He wants Tomoe broken, cleanly if the ground allows.

missionBrief.purchaseOptions: Between tracks (staged before the strike), an AFFS March high-command list — heavy and assault 'Mechs and the best combat vehicles, 2D6 of 7+. One assault on an 8+ (this is a Scale-3 job; bring weight).

tracks.name: Descent on New Pontiac
tracks.situation:
You come down fast and close on the assembly grounds outside New Pontiac — Tomoe's spearhead half-formed on the field below, machines mounting up, the whole thing a coiled spring not yet released. Speed is everything: hit the assembly before it can finish forming, break its cohesion, and drive a wedge toward its commander before the spearhead becomes the thing it was built to be. Let it complete and you are fighting a formed strike force on its own staging ground.

A strike is a scalpel swung hard — cut into the assembly, scatter the guard around the command element, and get your weight between Tomoe and the units she needs to lead. Corner her and the campaign's blade is at bay; let her rally the spearhead around herself and she slips the trap a third time and leaves you fighting the whole formation.
tracks.deployment: Short edges, assembly-ground map with New Pontiac's urban edge along one flank; the Combine (Defender) sets up spread across the field, still forming, Tomoe's command element toward the rear. You (Attacker) enter Turn 1. Assembly-alert rules in force.

objectives.text: Cut the Assembly — end Turn 4 with half your BV/PV inside the assembly ground (past the near guard).
Form the Spear — keep half the assembly ground clear of attacker units at end of Turn 4.
Corner the Blade — end a turn with a unit of yours within 4 hexes of Tomoe's unit and a clear line to it.
Rally the Guard — keep three or more Combine units within 6 hexes of Tomoe through Turn 5.
Scatter Them — reduce the near guard to half its starting BV/PV.

tracks.specialRules: If you corner the blade (score that objective) the Track-1 result opens the Duel branch; if Tomoe rallies her guard, she slips the trap and you fight the withdrawal. The higher-VP side sets Track 2's home edge and forces the loser to deploy first.
tracks.trackEnd: End of Turn 8 (Turn 8 AS).
tracks.salvagePolicy: Pool-draft (wrecks pooled, alternate picks, winner first).

forks.trigger: You cornered Tomoe against the burning assembly, and she has turned to face you.
forks.consequence: Answer her challenge — single combat while the field burns, blade against your best.

forks.trigger: Tomoe rallied the spearhead and slipped the wedge; the assembly is forming around you.
forks.consequence: Break off with what you shattered and fight clear before the spearhead completes.

tracks.name: The Sho-sa's Challenge
tracks.situation:
The assembly is scattered and burning, and Tomoe has stopped running. Across the smoke her No-Dachi stands square to your line, and over an open channel she offers the old answer of a Combine officer who has been beaten twice and will not be a third time by numbers alone: her machine against your best, blade to blade, while the two forces hold their fire and watch. It is honor and it is a trap and it is the only way she can leave this field with the spearhead's name intact — and if you take the challenge and win, you break Ishara's edge in front of everyone who will carry word of it.

A duel is a single clean fight in a ring the two armies make. Put your best pilot forward, hold the rest of your command to the line, and beat her on the ground she chose — but keep your discipline, because if your force breaks the challenge and swarms her, the watching spearhead is freed to fall on you and the honor you spent means nothing. Win it straight and Tomoe is finished as Ishara's blade; the storm that follows will have to be led by the Warlord himself.
tracks.deployment: A marked central arena (roughly 8 hexes across) between the two forces, both drawn up on opposite edges and holding fire. Your champion (one 'Mech, your pick) and Tomoe's No-Dachi enter the arena; the rest of both forces hold their edges. Assembly-alert rules in force outside the arena.

objectives.text: Answer the Challenge — your champion enters the arena and engages Tomoe in single combat.
Hold the Watch — keep the rest of your force on its edge, out of the arena, until the duel is decided.
Break the Blade — your champion destroys or forces the surrender of Tomoe's unit in the arena.
The Sho-sa Stands — Tomoe destroys or drives off your champion (your champion crippled or withdrawn).
With Honor — win the duel without any other unit of yours entering the arena.

tracks.specialRules: While the duel holds, both armies keep to their edges and do not fire. If any unit but the two champions enters the arena or opens fire, the challenge is broken: the watching spearhead is freed, the honor bonus is lost, and both forces engage (resolve as a Meeting Engagement from the edges). A won duel breaks Tomoe as a commander for Track 3 (the assembly cannot voluntarily withdraw).
tracks.trackEnd: The duel is decided (one champion destroyed, surrendered, or withdrawn), or the challenge is broken.
tracks.salvagePolicy: Winner-all of the duel (the victor claims the loser's machine as salvage per honor; SP at your salvage %).

forks.trigger: The duel is settled — with honor or in a broken challenge and a general fight.
forks.consequence: Finish the spearhead's assembly before Combine relief lands.

tracks.name: Break Off Clean
tracks.situation:
Tomoe rallied faster than you could close, and the spearhead is forming around your wedge instead of scattering before it — the trap you set is becoming the one you are in. There is no cornering her now; there is only leaving with what you already broke and keeping your command whole enough to matter at Mallory, where all of this is going anyway. A deep strike that trades itself away for nothing hands Ishara his edge and his propaganda both.

A clean break is a chosen lane and a hard rearguard. Pick the seam before the spearhead finishes closing, cover the withdrawal with your heaviest, and pull off the assembly ground with your teeth intact — and if the chance comes to put fire on Tomoe as you go, take it, because a wounded blade is a slower one. Break off whole and you still bled the spearhead and set the stage; get pinned on Marduk and the offensive opens with your command already spent.
tracks.deployment: Short edges, assembly-ground map; your force is in the center among the forming spearhead, the Combine (Defender) between you and the far (extraction) edge. You break Turn 1 toward the extraction edge. Assembly-alert rules in force.

objectives.text: Break Off — exit half your BV/PV off the extraction edge by Turn 8.
Close on Them — destroy or hold in place half the raiding force short of the edge.
Bring the Command Out — exit two-thirds of your force, including your commander's unit.
Pin the Raiders — reduce the raiders to half their starting BV/PV before they clear the edge.
Wound the Blade — cripple Tomoe's unit as you withdraw.

tracks.specialRules: A unit that exits the extraction edge is out (safe). Crippling Tomoe here carries into Track 3 (she fights the assembly's defense at reduced effect).
tracks.trackEnd: End of Turn 8 (Turn 8 AS), or your force has exited/been destroyed.
tracks.salvagePolicy: Defender-none; attacker keeps only what it tows off the extraction edge (SP at your salvage %).

forks.trigger: You pulled off the assembly ground, whole or bloodied.
forks.consequence: Turn back for one last push to shatter the assembly before relief lands and the window closes.

tracks.name: Shatter the Spearhead
tracks.situation:
The duel is done or the withdrawal is made, and one thing is left before the window closes: put the spearhead's assembly beyond use before Combine relief burns in from the jump point. Whatever happened to Tomoe, the units she was to lead are still on the field, and every one you break here is one that cannot open Ishara's offensive. This is the last blow of the long road that started on the Le Blanc flats — land it, and the storm that comes will have to be the Warlord's own.

An assault against the clock is weight thrown with a purpose. Drive into the assembly, wreck its formations and its heavy units, and reduce it past the point where it can lead anything — then be gone before the relief arrives to trap you on Marduk. Shatter the spearhead and you have armed the March for the Reckoning at Mallory; leave it whole and the offensive still has its edge when it falls on the border.
tracks.deployment: Short edges, assembly-ground map; the Combine (Defender) forms up around its remaining heavy units, Combine relief approaching the far edge (arrives end of Turn 6). You (Attacker) enter Turn 1. Assembly-alert and city-edge rules in force.

objectives.text: Into the Assembly — end Turn 3 with half your BV/PV inside the assembly ground.
Hold Until Relief — keep half the assembly's BV/PV intact and on the field until relief lands (end of Turn 6).
Break the Spear — reduce the spearhead's assembly below half its starting BV/PV.
Save the Spear — hold the assembly above half strength when relief arrives.
Gone Before the Gate — begin exiting the field the turn relief lands (no attacker unit destroyed by relief).

tracks.specialRules: Combine relief enters the far edge end of Turn 6; the track ends when relief is fully on the field. Reducing the assembly below half (with Tomoe broken) resolves the contract's break-the-spear victory and arms the campaign endgame.
tracks.trackEnd: End of Turn 8 (Turn 8 AS), or Combine relief has fully deployed.
tracks.salvagePolicy: Winner-all of the assembly (you keep what you tow off before relief closes the field; SP at your salvage %).

forks.trigger: The spearhead is shattered, or it held until relief landed.
forks.consequence: Contract closes — settle the March's pay and, if you broke the spear, the endgame bonus. The offensive has lost its edge; Tai-shu Ishara will lead the storm himself, and it falls on Mallory's World. The Reckoning is at hand.
